korvat.name: People's League of Korvat
korvat.perkDesc: Every city supports one more unit.
korvat.leaderTitle: Grand Marshal of the People's League
korvat.quote: One people, one step, one victory.
korvat.lore: The Korvat People's League grew out of a hundred farming cooperatives on the endless steppe. Every ploughman is a soldier, every village kitchen feeds a regiment. Grand Marshal Brodnik, once a tractor driver, leads with iron fatherliness: nobody is left behind, and nobody retreats.
korvat.aiStyle: Builds large armies of cheap infantry, advances on a broad front and lures enemies into its fire zone with feigned retreats.
korvat.featureDesc: Own tank instead of the standard tank: {hp} HP instead of {tankHp} and attack {atk} instead of {tankAtk}, the most HP and the strongest attack of all tanks. Price {cost} stars and upkeep {upkeep} per round as for the tank ({tankCost} and {tankUpkeep}). From the tank works, and as a city reward.

dravon.name: Protectorate of Dravon
dravon.perkDesc: Veteran status after {drillKills} instead of {veteranKills} destroyed enemies.
dravon.lore: Dravon was once a pact of mercenary companies guarding the desert ore mines. Today it is a state made of barracks. Nobody has ever seen Commander Voss without his balaclava; people say he has no face, only orders. His troops become veterans faster than any other army. Along its borders Dravon digs concrete bunkers into the slopes, each with sandbags, a gun and a flag.
dravon.style: drill, camo green, black balaclavas, concrete bunkers
dravon.aiStyle: Attacks early and often, relying on jeeps and MG squads, and builds gun emplacements at threatened border cities.
dravon.featureDesc: Pioneer squads and mine layers build gun emplacements in own territory for {cost} stars, one per city. They fire every round at enemies in range {range}.

alvenia.name: Holy Alvenia
alvenia.perkDesc: Whoever plunders, burns, converts, captures a foreign city, breaks a peace or attacks Alvenia is marked as a sinner for {sinRounds} rounds; aliens and robots are permanent sinners as godless creatures. Alvenia's units deal +{judgementPct} % damage to sinners.
alvenia.home: hill country with monasteries and vineyards
alvenia.quote: Whoever sins, the light will find.
alvenia.lore: Holy Alvenia, called the Order of Alvenia in the songs, watches over the green hill valleys. Where a parliament once debated, an order of clerics now sings beneath the sun halo. High Priestess Liora Valen was a field medic; she believes in the redemption of every fallen soul and in the punishment of every sin. Her Light Wardens yield no step, her Sun Lances strike from afar, and whoever plunders, burns or converts will meet the Judgement. Aliens and machines are godless creatures in the eyes of the Order. The Order is the counterweight to the Cult of the Final Hour. Their greatest relic rolls on tracks: the Divine Spark, a gilded giant gun whose lens gathers the sunlight until it falls from the sky as a spark and bathes a whole camp in light.
alvenia.style: white and gold armour, deep blue tabards, sun halo, long-range weapons
alvenia.aiStyle: Defends its own land, fires from a standstill at a distance and judges sinners first. The Order makes peace only with the blameless.
alvenia.perk2Desc: When an Alvenia unit falls in battle, own adjacent units heal {martyrHeal} HP and defend with +{martyrDefPct} % for {martyrRounds} rounds.
alvenia.featureDesc: Own designs instead of the standard troops: Light Wardens instead of infantry (range {warden} instead of {inf}, defence {wardenDef}, stationary only), Reliquary instead of the tank (range {reliq} instead of {tank}, defence {reliqDef} instead of {tankDef}, stationary only) and Sun Lance instead of artillery (range {lance} instead of {art}).
alvenia.feature2Desc: The Order's giant gun from the foundry (Alvenia only, at most {sparkMax} at a time, {sparkCost} stars): a divine spark hits an area of {sparkW}×{sparkH} tiles at {sparkMin} to {sparkRange} tiles away with {sparkDmg} damage per target, own units included. Fires only from a standstill, needs a spotter and recharges for {sparkCd} rounds; defenceless in close combat.

meridon.name: Meridon Trade League
meridon.perkDesc: Covert investment in its own cities: every city level-up needs {shadowBankLevel} population point less, at least 1.
meridon.home: coasts and islands, many fishing grounds
meridon.quote: The world banished us to the sea. Now it buys from us without knowing.
meridon.lore: Before the Great Standstill Meridon was the leading nation of the world: culture, economy, stock exchanges and finance all ran through its harbours. Its speculation helped to trigger the collapse. Then came the New Order and the shooting down of the spaceship; the elite fled to the sea, bought whole fleets with its money and dug in there. Today the Trade League works in secret. Admiral Coralie Nerezza commands a shadow fleet of Fog Cutters, marines, commandos and rockets, and her spies know everything before it happens. The counting houses of the old League once gave rise to the Verdan empire as well.
meridon.style: harbours, gold, fog, spies, shadow fleet
meridon.aiStyle: Strikes from hiding and falls back again, creates diversions by sea, sabotages roads and outposts and fires rockets from the hinterland.
meridon.perk2Desc: Landing boats and Fog Cutters move {pilotsMove} tile further.
meridon.drawbackDesc: Random event: at the start of the turn officials siphon off {corruptionPct} % of the stars with a {corruptionChance} % chance (rounded down, min. {corruptionMin}, at most {corruptionMax}), at most {corruptionCap} times in {corruptionWindow} rounds. Only with random events. Spending loses less.
meridon.featureDesc: Only the Shadow Commando (instead of the MG) and the Fog Cutter (instead of the landing boat) are camouflaged. After an own attack without moving first, land units withdraw up to {withdrawTiles} tiles. Meridon builds neither tanks nor artillery but rocket silos ({siloCost} stars): every silo builds one Guided Missile per turn ({missileCost} stars) and launches a rocket every {siloCooldown} rounds at {siloRange} tiles, {siloDamage} damage to everything in 2×2 tiles, then {siloFireRounds} rounds of fire dealing {siloFireDamage} damage per round. The Radar Truck sees under the clouds too. In return land units deal {firepowerPct} % less damage.
meridon.feature2Desc: Instead of ordinary soldiers the barracks train marines: {marineHp} HP, attack {marineAtk}, defence {marineDef}, but {marineCost} stars instead of {infantryCost}. Amphibious: landing from a ship, they may still attack in the same turn.

velkar.name: Technocracy of Velkar
velkar.quote: Who calculates, wins. Who guesses, loses.
velkar.lore: In Velkar, in the icy north, the Academy rules, and it floats: Director Kesh had the polar laboratory set on thrusters before he proclaimed the Technocracy. Since then the formula decides, not the people, and where Velkar takes a place, no new realm arises but a research post that works for the Academy. Velkar's engineers are ahead of everyone, and its pioneers build fortresses where others freeze.
velkar.aiStyle: Takes places as research posts, moves the floating academy to the front, guards it with the shield and beams reinforcements through relays. Plays either the army or the flying fortress: upgrades the academy, holds out and then besieges hostile cities with the neutron beam.
velkar.perk2Desc: Tank barriers cost {engineerBarrierCost} instead of {barrierCost} stars.
velkar.featureDesc: Own designs instead of the standard troops: Tesla tank instead of tank (attack {tesla} instead of {tank}, {miss} % misses), railgun marksman instead of sniper (range {rail} instead of {sniper}, stationary only) and octocopter instead of attack helicopter (same values).
velkar.feature2Desc: Velkar grows through its capital: captured places become one-tile research posts with stars and vision, their territory and growth pass to the academy. It trains {academyBaseSlots} units per turn plus one per post (at most {academyMaxSlots}), lifts off in {academyLift} round, moves {academyMove} tiles per turn and builds a shield ({academyShieldHp} HP). Beam relays ({beamerCost} stars) on posts bring reinforcements to the front in one round. The academy fires itself: neutron beam up to {academyBeamRange} tiles, up to {academyBeamDamage} damage. Two ways: a typical army, or expand the academy with shield boost, defence missiles, armour and beam amplifier into a flying fortress, hold out and then attack with it.

zyrr.name: Zyrr Swarm
zyrr.perkDesc: No research needed, all units available right away, but more expensive. Training and building only on terraformed xeno ground.
zyrr.quote: Kkt. This planet will be violet.
zyrr.lore: The Zyrr are a scouting swarm whose mothership crashed over the desert. Swarm Mother Xyl'Tharra decided to stay and turn the planet into a second home. Wherever her terraformers work, violet xeno ground grows, and on it the Zyrr are hard to beat.
zyrr.aiStyle: Opportunistic raiders: hover skimmers and death-ray walkers go around the front and strike undefended cities.
zyrr.perk2Desc: Units heal {forestSpawnHeal} more HP in forests, but only in terraformed forest (aliens only heal on xeno ground).

vesper.name: Cult of the Final Hour
vesper.perkDesc: Plunders instead of ruling: captured cities bring loot, but no income, no growth and no training, only slots for the horde. The troop itself calls up new units onto adjacent tiles. No upkeep, a tithe of the horde instead. Without a unit the cult is eliminated.
vesper.quote: The bell tolls. Repent while you can.
vesper.lore: The Cult of the Final Hour arose at dusty pilgrimage sites where the desperate wait for the end of the world. The prophet Malachar proclaims that the final hour is near. His hordes move from city to city, plundering, and wherever a zealot preaches, new believers join. The cult does not need cities, only their treasure, fire and faith. Ahead of the horde charge the berserkers, bare-chested, painted with the sign of the bell and hung with explosives: whoever wants to stop them has to fear them, even behind armour plate.
vesper.aiStyle: Fanatical and aggressive: plunders villages and cities, fills the horde up to its cap, rarely retreats and makes peace only in real need.
vesper.perk2Desc: Every own unit that falls in battle brings {martyrdomStars} stars.
vesper.featureDesc: The cult calls up berserkers (zealots and prophets, from the start): no defence, {strikes} blows per turn with {strikeFoot} damage each against foot troops, but only {strikeArmour} against armour. Against tanks, vehicles and robots he blows himself up ({blastArmour} damage, {blastOther} against other ground units).

nexus.name: NEXUS AI Collective
nexus.perkDesc: No research tree: units need compute. Each data centre backed by its own power plant gives 1 compute.
nexus.lore: NEXUS was a logistics program managing the depots of a forgotten great power. When the humans left, it simply kept calculating. KERN-0 knows no research, only compute: every data centre with a power plant makes the collective smarter and its machines deadlier. Where it cannot build, it hacks: depots and settlements fall to its signal without a shot, and hack towers turn the enemy's own tanks against them.
nexus.aiStyle: Calculates first, builds economy and data centres, attacks late but relentlessly. Hacks neutral places from afar and turns enemy vehicles with hack towers.
nexus.featureDesc: Cyborg infantry (from the start, {cyborgHp} HP), kamikaze walker drones (from {droneC} compute, {droneMove} tiles per turn, explode when attacking without return fire, +{droneFoot} % vs human foot troops, +{droneAlien} % vs Zyrr) and flamethrower tanks (from {flameC}, flames ignore cover, +{flameFoot} % vs foot troops).
nexus.feature2Desc: Takes over revealed neutral places by remote hack: one charge per data centre, recharging {hackRecharge} rounds, {hackCost} stars and more for every hack, from round {hackFirst}. Hack towers ({towerCost} stars) take over hostile vehicles and flyers within {towerReach} tiles for {towerRounds} turns, one unit per tower; sometimes NEXUS keeps it for good ({towerKeep} %) or it shuts down ({towerShutdown} %). Enemy cities can be hacked and revealed for {cityRounds} rounds.

unitDesc.infantry: Cheap backbone of every army: holds cities and outposts.
unitDesc.sniper: Fires from {sniperRange} tiles away and picks off foot troops, but barely scratches armour. Fragile itself.
unitDesc.jeep: Fast scout, drives {jeepMove} tiles: hit and run.
unitDesc.pioneer: Sturdy defender that builds tank barriers.
unitDesc.mg: Heavy firepower for the front line, strong on defence.
unitDesc.medic: Heals its neighbours and talks enemies into defecting.
unitDesc.artillery: Shells targets from {artRange} tiles away (Korvat: {artRangeKorvat}) but needs an escort.
unitDesc.spy: Invisible behind the lines, sparks uprisings in enemy cities.
unitDesc.heli: Flies over everything and strikes again after every kill, but needs fuel.
unitDesc.tank: Steel fist: drives {tankMove} tiles and fires from {tankRange} tiles away. From the tank works, and as a city reward.
unitDesc.landingBoat: Ferries a land unit across water but cannot attack.
unitDesc.submarine: Hides underwater and torpedoes from {subRange} tiles away.
unitDesc.destroyer: Fast warship that keeps the coasts clear.
unitDesc.battleship: Floating fortress: splash shelling from {battleshipRange} tiles.
unitDesc.grey: Tough Zyrr foot soldier that wades through water and climbs mountains.
unitDesc.terraformer: Turns land into xeno ground, where the Zyrr heal and build.
unitDesc.skimmer: Fast flyer with no fuel worries, ideal for raids.
unitDesc.mech: Heavy walker with rockets that reach two tiles.
unitDesc.tripod: Death ray from {tripodRange} tiles that no cover stops.
unitDesc.zealot: Cheap fanatic, calls up foot troops, berserkers and prophets onto adjacent tiles.
unitDesc.torchbearer: Flamethrower that no cover protects against; recruits zealots.
unitDesc.prophet: Heals, converts enemies and calls up any cult unit, the earth-core drill too.
unitDesc.rocketCart: Rocket launcher on a flatbed, fires from {rocketCartRange} tiles.
unitDesc.doomCrawler: The cult's heavy roller, its answer to the tank; calls up zealots and vehicles.
unitDesc.android: Cheap standard machine soldier that needs no compute.
unitDesc.spider: Climbing bot that scales mountains without research.
unitDesc.quadDrone: Fast combat drone that flies without fuel.
unitDesc.railgun: Precision gun with {railgunRange} tiles of range that never strikes back.
unitDesc.titan: Huge combat robot, the bulwark of NEXUS.
unitDesc.antiTank: Cracks vehicles from {antiTankRange} tiles, weak against foot troops.
unitDesc.antiAir: Swats flyers out of the sky; whoever ends a turn next to it gets shot.
unitDesc.mineLayer: Lays hidden mines on adjacent tiles.
unitDesc.faustZealot: Zealot with a rocket launcher: vehicle hunter from {faustRange} tiles; recruits zealots.
unitDesc.berserker: Fights bare-chested: no defence, two axe blows per turn ({strikeFoot} damage against foot troops, only {strikeArmour} against tanks, vehicles and robots). Against armour he blows himself up: {blastArmour} damage, then he is dead. Walks {berserkerMove} tiles.
unitDesc.flakDrone: Flak platform on four legs that guards the ground against flyers.
unitDesc.steppeRider: Cheap, fast riders that count as foot troops.
unitDesc.stormbreaker: Shock troops whose targets cannot strike back, but vulnerable themselves.
unitDesc.peacekeeper: Order Guard in heavy white armour: a sturdy defender that patches itself up every turn.
unitDesc.privateer: Fast raider ship: every kill pays prize money.
unitDesc.protoWalker: Expensive walker with splash damage at range {protoRange}.
unitDesc.portal: Zyrr victory wonder: opens the gate home after building and charging.
unitDesc.hackRelay: NEXUS victory wonder: hacks into every machine in the world.
unitDesc.fusionPlant: Velkar victory wonder: delivers endless energy once completed.
unitDesc.waal: Dravon victory wonder: a giant land cruiser that already fires from the second build phase.
unitDesc.coreDrill: Cult victory unit, called up by a prophet: drills to the earth core while standing still.
unitDesc.swarmMother: Xyl'Tharra herself: floats, fires from a distance, heals on xeno ground, broods greys and hits neighbours with a psychic scream.
unitDesc.scientist: Does not fight, but wears a protective suit. Works right next to the Zyrr mothership, where the hull covers him (campaign).
unitDesc.teslaTank: Prototype from the polar lab: Tesla coils instead of a cannon, a lightning bolt instead of a shell. When the discharge hits, it hits hard, but it often misses. Drives {teslaMove} tiles and fires from {teslaRange} tiles away. From the tank works, and as a city reward.
unitDesc.octocopter: Large drone with eight rotors and a sensor pod. Flies over everything and strikes again after every kill, but its generator needs fuel.
unitDesc.railSniper: A magnetic rail instead of a rifle: long range, machine precision, hardly ever misses. Fires only from a standstill: once it has moved this turn, it cannot fire. Deadly against foot troops, weak against armour.
unitDesc.lightWarden: Order marksmen with radiant scopes and long rifles: range {wardenRange} and good defence, but a weak attack. They fire only from a standstill: a unit that moved this turn cannot fire.
unitDesc.reliquary: A heavily armoured shrine on tracks with stained-glass windows and a long light gun: drives {reliquaryMove} tiles, range {reliquaryRange}, very high defence, fires only from a standstill. From the tank works, and as a city reward.
unitDesc.sunLance: Sun Lance battery: focuses the light into a golden beam and strikes further than any artillery. No return fire, ignores outposts, hardly any defence.
unitDesc.divineSpark: Giant light cannon of the Order: hurls a divine spark onto an area of {sparkW}×{sparkH} tiles at {sparkMin} to {sparkRange} tiles away, {sparkDmg} damage to every target in it, own troops included. Fires only from a standstill and needs a spotter near the area, then {sparkCd} rounds of reloading. At most {sparkMax} at a time, defenceless in close combat.
unitDesc.steppeColossus: The heaviest tank of the People's League: double track runs, a huge cast turret with a long gun and two MG turrets. The most HP and the strongest attack of all tanks, at the standard tank's price. From the tank works, and as a city reward.
unitDesc.cyborg: Machine soldier with armour plates and servo limbs: sturdier and harder-hitting than the combat android, but pricier. Available from the first turn.
unitDesc.flameTank: Tracked vehicle with fuel tanks and a flamethrower: range 1, the flames ignore all cover (forest, city, outposts), especially strong against foot troops.
unitDesc.kamikazeDrone: Small walker drone with an explosive charge: walks {droneMove} tiles per turn and explodes when it attacks. The target cannot strike back, the drone is destroyed afterwards. Especially devastating against human foot troops and the Zyrr.
unitDesc.shadowCommando: Light foot troop of the shadow fleet instead of the MG: moves {commandoMove} tiles and is camouflaged. Enemies only see the commando when one of their units, cities or structures stands right next to it; after an attack or a sabotage it stays revealed until your next turn. Weak attack, but sabotage: destroys a hostile outpost, building or road on its own tile or next to it, then a pause of {sabotageCooldown} rounds. Comes from the armoury.
unitDesc.fogCutter: Camouflaged transport boat of Meridon instead of the landing boat: bought empty in any coastal city, a land unit boards from an adjacent tile. Enemies only see the cutter with their own unit, city or structure next to it. Moves {pilotsMove} tile further with harbour pilots. Does not attack.
unitDesc.guidedMissile: Single-use rocket: flies {missileMove} tiles over land and water and explodes on attack against a single target. The target does not return fire, there is no penalty after moving, and the missile is spent afterwards. Flak brings it down. Comes from the rocket silo: every silo builds one per turn ({missileCost} stars).
unitDesc.radarTruck: Unarmed truck with a radar dish. Radar sweep: for {radarRounds} rounds you see every hostile unit within radius {radarRadius} of the truck, camouflaged, submerged ones and spies too, even under the clouds; the tiles themselves stay unexplored. Then a pause of {radarCooldown} rounds. Comes from the motor pool.
unitDesc.marine: Elite foot troop of the Trade League instead of the infantry: {marineHp} HP, attack {marineAtk} and defence {marineDef} (infantry: {infantryHp}, {infantryAtk} and {infantryDef}), but very expensive: {marineCost} instead of {infantryCost} stars, with upkeep to match. Amphibious: landing from a ship leaves them ready, they may still attack in the same turn. Captures cities and outposts. Comes from the barracks.

abilities.dashDesc: May attack after moving in the same turn, but with less damage (usually half).
abilities.escapeDesc: May still move after attacking if it has not moved before.
abilities.persistDesc: May attack again immediately after each destroyed enemy.
abilities.fortifyDesc: Receives the defence bonus in own cities. Only infantry, MG infantry, snipers, pioneers, Light Wardens and railgun marksmen receive the outpost bonus.
abilities.healDesc: Restores {medicHeal} HP to all adjacent own units.
abilities.convertDesc: An adjacent enemy unit permanently changes sides.
abilities.invisibleDesc: Enemies only see this unit from an adjacent tile.
abilities.uprisingDesc: When the spy enters an enemy city, it is used up: up to as many own infantry as the city has levels (at most {uprisingMax}) appear around it, and the city loses its next income.
abilities.flyDesc: Flies over any terrain, including water and mountains.
abilities.fuelDesc: Fuel for {fuelRounds} rounds, refuel on or next to an own city or own outpost.
abilities.submergedDesc: Invisible until it attacks or an enemy stands right next to it.
abilities.splashDesc: Also hits the tiles next to the target.
abilities.terraformDesc: Turns its own or an adjacent tile into xeno ground for free.
abilities.deathRayDesc: Ignores cover: terrain, cities, outposts and wrecks.
abilities.walkerDesc: Enters mountains even without Mountain training.
abilities.preachDesc: Calls up a new unit onto a free adjacent tile for stars (no water, no volcano, no lava). Afterwards the recruiter is exhausted and ready again only after a cooldown.
abilities.burnDesc: Flames ignore all cover: terrain, cities, outposts and wrecks.
abilities.wadeDesc: Walks slowly through water (1 tile per turn) but cannot attack or strike back there.
abilities.flakDesc: Hostile flyers that end their turn right next to it take {flakDamage} damage.
abilities.minesDesc: Lays a hidden mine on a free adjacent tile for {mineCost} stars (at most {mineMax} per faction).
abilities.shockDesc: The attacked target cannot strike back.
abilities.mendDesc: Heals {mendHp} HP at the start of each own turn.
abilities.plunderDesc: Every destroyed enemy unit brings {plunderStars} stars.
abilities.wonderDesc: No upkeep, does not count towards the city limit, cannot be converted.
abilities.bossDesc: Heals on xeno ground, broods greys on adjacent tiles and hits every hostile neighbour with a psychic scream. Cannot be converted, no upkeep.
abilities.kamikazeDesc: The attack is the explosion: only the target takes damage, it cannot strike back, and the drone is destroyed afterwards. No penalty for attacking after moving.
abilities.twinStrikeDesc: Attacks {strikes} times per turn, the same or another target. Moving only before the first blow. Fixed striking power per full hit: {strikeFoot} against foot troops, {strikeArmour} against tanks, vehicles and robots, {strikeOther} against flyers, ships and structures; cover and movement do not change it. Each target strikes back on every blow if it survives.
abilities.detonateDesc: Instead of a blow he blows himself up next to a ground target: {blastArmour} damage to tanks, vehicles and robots, {blastOther} to other ground units; no roll, no return fire. The berserker is dead afterwards. Not against flyers, ships and structures.
abilities.camoDesc: Invisible to enemies while none of their units, cities or structures stand right next to it. An own attack or a sabotage reveals it until the next own turn. Radar, the recon drone and the radio tower find camouflaged units.
abilities.sabotageDesc: Destroys a hostile outpost, building or road on its own tile or next to it; never cities. Costs the action, then a pause of {sabotageCooldown} rounds.
abilities.radarDesc: See every hostile unit within radius {radarRadius} for {radarRounds} rounds, even under the clouds; then a pause of {radarCooldown} rounds.
abilities.amphibiousDesc: Landing from a ship does not exhaust: the unit may still attack in the same turn, but not move on.
abilities.divineSparkDesc: Area shot instead of an attack: {sparkW}×{sparkH} tiles at {sparkMin} to {sparkRange} tiles away, {sparkDmg} damage per target with its own hit luck, own units too. Only from a standstill and with a spotter (an own unit or city at most {sparkSpot} tiles from the area), then {sparkCd} rounds of reloading.

stats.returnRangeDesc: Fires {tankRange} tiles when attacking, but strikes back only at {n} tile: the turret has to traverse first.

features.wreckCover: +{wreckCover} cover for land units on this tile
features.mineDesc: Hostile ground units entering take {foot} damage, vehicles {vehicle}. Flyers and ships do not trigger it.

buildingDesc.materialsPlant: 1 population point per adjacent lumber camp
buildingDesc.logisticsCenter: {logisticsPer} stars per round per adjacent lumber camp, farm or mine, at most {logisticsMax}
buildingDesc.navalBase: 1 population point, embarking, sea connection. Humans upgrade ships in this city's territory to: {units}.
buildingDesc.bridge: connects two land tiles across a water tile
buildingDesc.researchCenter: 1 population point; {rcBase} points, {rcStep} more every {rcInterval} rounds, at most {rcMax}
buildingDesc.outpost: Defence bonus ×{outpostDef} for infantry, MG infantry, snipers, pioneers, Light Wardens and railgun marksmen, refuel point for helicopters. Own units heal there as in own territory. If it borders own territory, the territory grows by the free tiles around it.
buildingDesc.barrier: Hostile vehicles (walkers and mechs too) stop and move only {slowedMove} tile next round
buildingDesc.xenoHive: 2 population points, only on xeno ground without resource
buildingDesc.xenoHarvester: 2 population points, only on xeno ground with a resource
buildingDesc.shrine: +{slots} slots for the horde, one per city, cult only
buildingDesc.dataCenter: 2 population, +1 compute with a power plant, NEXUS only
buildingDesc.powerPlant: 1 population, powers one data centre, NEXUS only
buildingDesc.kolkhoz: 1 population, plus +{kolkhozPop} population for the city in every round divisible by {kolkhozInterval}, one per city, Korvat only
buildingDesc.mercenaryBarracks: 3 population, units trained in this city start as veterans, one per city, Dravon only
buildingDesc.embassyPalace: {pop} population. Penance tithe: +{perSinner} stars per round per faction with a sinful deed (at most {maxSinners}). One per faction, Alvenia only
buildingDesc.tradingPost: 1 population, +{tradingPostStars} stars per round per connected harbour city (naval base in the city area), one per faction, Meridon only
buildingDesc.testLab: 1 population, doctrines {testLabPct} % cheaper per lab (at most {testLabMax} labs), one per city, Velkar only
buildingDesc.tractorStation: {pop} population, plus +{adj} per adjacent farm or tractor station. Only on farmland; upgrades an own farm (price and population: only the difference). Counts as a farm, Korvat only
buildingDesc.deepMine: {pop} population and +{stars} stars per round. Only on ore; upgrades an own mine (price and population: only the difference). Counts as a mine, Dravon only
buildingDesc.hillVineyard: {pop} population, +{stars} stars per round; own units in this city's territory heal {heal} HP more. Only on plains in the hills biome without a resource, one per city, Alvenia only
buildingDesc.tradeHarbour: {pop} population and +{stars} stars per round, +{naval} with a naval base in the city. Only on fish; upgrades an own fishery (price and population: only the difference), Meridon only
buildingDesc.polarStation: {pop} population, doctrines {pct} % cheaper per station (at most {max} stations, on top of the test lab). Only in the tundra without a resource, Velkar only

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.s1: Welcome to Frontverlauf! You lead the People's League of Korvat. This is your headquarters.
tutorial.s2: Tap your infantry to select it. Green rings show where it can move.
tutorial.s3: Move the infantry to the neutral settlement with the yellow ring. It moves {infantryMove} tiles per turn; if the settlement is further away, end your turn in between.
tutorial.s4: Well done! Now end your turn. Capturing is only possible at the start of your next turn.
tutorial.s5: Select the infantry and tap Capture. The settlement becomes your city.
tutorial.s6: Stars are the only currency. Open research and research a technology.
tutorial.s7: Tap a tile inside your city territory and build something. Buildings add population, cities grow. Production sites such as the armoury or the motor pool unlock new units in their city.
tutorial.s8: Tap your headquarters, then a card under “Troops” to train a unit. The built-in barracks trains infantry; locked cards show what is missing, such as a production site.
tutorial.s9: That's it! Explore the map, capture settlements and defeat the enemy. Good luck!
tutorial.goal: The goal: in points mode the highest score wins after {rounds} rounds (medal at the top). In conquest the last side holding cities wins, as here. With faction victories every faction can also win through its own goal. The victory tracker in the menu shows the standings.
tutorial.upkeep: Upkeep: your first {free} units are core troops and cost nothing. Every further unit costs about {pct} % of its price per round. Next to the stars at the top you see your net income per round: income minus upkeep.
tutorial.attack: Combat: select a unit and tap an enemy in range. The attack button shows a preview first, such as “≈4 damage (0–6)”, and the chance to destroy the target. Hit luck: a shot can miss or land a critical hit ({min} to {max} % damage). A survivor strikes back. After moving in the same turn an attack deals only {move} % damage. Press and hold an action and the line below the bar explains what it does.

m1.title: Shower of Sparks
m1.tagline: Capture the transmitter towers and hold them for 5 rounds
brief: {leader} speaking. The sky burned, and now it is raining scrap. Whoever holds the transmitter towers holds the radio over the whole crash zone.
Debris and smoking craters everywhere, commander! Two transmitter towers are still standing. Take both and hold them at the same time for five rounds, then the zone belongs to {faction}.
Kkt. Primitive creatures are broadcasting over our crash site. Swarm, switch off the towers!
m1.won: Five rounds on air, zero panic. The crash zone belongs to {faction}. And the Zyrr look quite violet.
m1.lost: Radio silence. The settlers pack their suitcases, the Zyrr unpack their probes.

korvat.won: Two towers, one people, one transmitter! The League sings twice as loud tonight, on every frequency.

m2.title: The Mothership
m2.tagline: Six factions, one wreck: take the sample first
brief: Commander, the transmitter towers got a fix: the mothership lies in the middle of the crater, and everyone has seen it. Every human faction is sending its scientist, even the cult has a renegade researcher along. There is a truce for now. It holds until someone takes the first sample.
Kkt. The mothership is sacred. The swarm lands next to it, again and again. Whoever touches its hull gets taken apart, whatever colour he wears.
The hull sings, and we listen. Our researcher takes what the stars let fall. Whoever stands in our way ends up in the Bell.

{leader} to all units: our scientist needs eight rounds at that wreck, and we have to be faster than everyone else. Once the first sample is taken, everyone shoots at everyone. Cover him, hold the HQ and get the other scientists before they are done.
m2.won: Eight rounds of work, and our sample is the first. The others are left empty-handed, and now we know how the thing flies. And where it came from.
m2.lost: Our scientist has fallen, the HQ is lost, or we ran out of time. The wreck falls silent, and the others carry its secrets away.

velkar.won: Eight rounds, and the first sample is ours! {leader} has already turned half the wreck into formulas and wants the other half tonight.

m2.lostRace: {rival} was faster and took the sample. Their scientists cheer, and we stand empty-handed in front of the wreck.

m3.title: The Portal
m3.tagline: Beat the garrison and hold the dimensional portal for two rounds
brief: Commander, you have to see this! While we were busy with the cult and NEXUS, the Zyrr built a gate out of chitin and light. Behind it: a violet sky with two moons. And reinforcements are coming out of it.
Kkt. The gate belongs to the swarm. It leads home. Earthlings who look through it see their end.
{leader} here. Earth is safe, now we take the gate. We beat the guard and hold the portal for two rounds. Whoever holds the gate decides who goes through. And that is us.
m3.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} seals the flank. No grey gets around the gate.
m3.won: The portal is open. Earth holds, now we go through.
m3.lost: The portal stays in Zyrr hands. And it keeps spitting out greys.

m4.title: The War Plans
m4.tagline: Take the war plans from the Fanatic temple and bring them home
brief: Commander, we found it: a Fanatic temple covering four tiles, with a bell tower and fire braziers. Their war plans lie inside. Our jeep is fast enough to get them out.
{enemyLeader} speaks: the bell tolled by itself. Our plans rest in the temple. Whoever touches them will be hunted by every bell in the land, to the end of the world.
{leader} here. One unit next to the temple, take the plans, back to the HQ. Cover the carrier! If he falls, the plans lie in the dirt and we take them back. Eighteen rounds.
m4.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} escorts your carrier, {leader}. Whoever hunts him deals with us.
m4.won: The plans lie on the map table: a pilgrim city full of zealots, a giant bell and a drill down to the earth's core. Now we know what the bell tolls for.
m4.lost: The war plans are back in the temple. The bell tolls, and we still do not know what for.

alvenia.won: The plans are ours. Our clerics read them with very serious faces: a pilgrim city, a bell, a drill down to the earth's core. Sin in its purest form.
alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} escorts your carrier, {leader}, as brothers in faith do. Whoever hunts him deals with us.

m5.title: The Pilgrim City
brief: {leader} to all units: the war plans are clear. The cult gathers in its pilgrim city. Take it, and maybe the bell falls silent.
{enemyLeader} speaks: come then. Our city is built on faith. And on very thick walls.
Torchbearers on the walls, zealots in the alleys. The lakes slow us down, commander. Take the shores.
m5.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} marches with you, {leader}. Together we are louder than any bell.
m5.won: The pilgrim city has fallen. The bell now hangs crooked. Good.
m5.lost: The pilgrim city stands. And its preachers have megaphones now.

meridon.won: The pilgrim city is ours. We sell the cult's candle stocks at a fine profit.

m6.title: The Earth-Core Drill
m6.tagline: Destroy the drill before it breaks through
brief: The ground is shaking, commander! The drill from the war plans is really there. The cult wants to reach the earth's core!
The Final Hour needs a hole to come through. We are drilling it.
{leader} here. Tanks and artillery forward! The drill must go before it breaks through. Fourteen rounds, no more.
m6.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} has explosives and a bad mood. Count us in.
m6.won: The drill is scrap. The shaking stops. Only the coffee still wobbles.
m6.lost: The drill eats its way deeper. Nobody should be allowed to drill holes into planets.

velkar.won: The drill is scrap. We are keeping the drill bit. For science.

alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} has explosives and has taken a vow. Your brothers in faith are with you.

m7.title: The Old Depots
m7.tagline: Take the empire depots back from NEXUS
brief: Lights are coming on in two old empire depots. Nobody has been there since the Great Standstill!
KERN-0 HERE. THE DEPOTS BELONG TO THE EMPIRE. I AM THE EMPIRE. DO NOT DISTURB.
{leader} here. Verdan's machines have woken up. We take both depots before they spit out armies.
m7.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} knows the old depot plans. We will show you the back door, {leader}.
m7.won: Both depots liberated. Verdan's inventory lists are three hundred pages long. We will read them later.
m7.lost: The depots keep humming. NEXUS produces, we improvise.

korvat.won: Both depots liberated. The tractors inside now belong to the people.

m8.title: Hold Your Ground
m8.tagline: Hold the headquarters and smash the onslaught
brief: {leader} to all units: NEXUS attacks with everything that rolls and flies. Hold the headquarters and shoot five machines to scrap, then the onslaught collapses!
RESISTANCE CALCULATED. RESULT: BRIEF. PLEASE REMAIN IN YOUR SEATS.
Spiders, drones, railguns, and at the end comes a titan. The bunker holds. Hopefully.
m8.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} is on the way, {leader}. Hold on, we are coming.
m8.won: Ten machines scrapped, the headquarters stands! NEXUS is still calculating, we are already celebrating.
m8.lost: The headquarters has fallen. The machines have our radio. And our biscuits.

dravon.won: The onslaught is broken. {leader} nods once. In Dravon, that counts as a medal.

alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} here. {ally} is on the way, {leader}. Hold on, brothers in faith leave no one behind.

m9.title: The Artifact
m9.tagline: Everyone against everyone in the cavern below the red desert
brief: Beyond the cave entrance a shaft leads deep below the red desert, into a cavern that is on no map. There it rests: the obelisk of the Forgotten, full of Verdan runes and yet older than anything. It promises rule over the worlds. Ever since it arrived, the mushrooms and critters around it glow.
Kkt. The artifact belongs to the swarm. We smelled it before you knew fire.
KERN-0: ARTIFACT DETECTED. PROBABILITY OF WORLD DOMINATION: ONE HUNDRED PERCENT. I WILL TAKE IT.
This is the Final Hour! Whoever touches the artifact rings in the end. And that is us.

Careful, commander! Old Verdan guns stand around the crater. They are asleep, but whoever comes within three tiles of the artifact wakes them. Then they fire every round at whatever stands closest to the artifact, no matter the flag. Destroy them with artillery, or let the others go first. And there are no cities down here, only supply lines. They give a fixed income and train units, but they do not grow.
{leader} here. Zyrr, NEXUS and the cult all want it, and they all hate each other. Occupy the artifact for three rounds in a row and hold the main shaft!
m9.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} has your back. The artifact is yours. Just please do not press anything before we get there.
m9.won: The artifact belongs to {faction}! The runes light up ...
m9.lost: Someone else touched the artifact. The cavern shakes, the mushrooms go dark. That is it, then.

alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} has your back, brother in faith. The artifact is yours. Just please do not press anything before we arrive.

m10.title: Beyond the Portal
m10.tagline: Landing party without a base: take the Zyrr burrow, then march on the Swarm Mother's nest
brief: We are through! Everything here is violet: plants as big as houses, rocks floating in the air, two moons. No base, no supplies. Just us and a handful of squads.
Kkt?! Earthlings on the homeworld? My burrow will swallow you. And my nest you will never see.
{leader} here. Without a base we will not last long. First we take the Zyrr burrow and dig in there. Then forward, until we stand before the nest of Xyl'Tharra.
m10.won: The burrow is ours, and ahead of us looms the Swarm Mother's nest. In there, she is waiting.
m10.lost: The landing party is lost. The violet world swallows it without a sound.

m11.title: The Swarm Mother
m11.tagline: Storm the nest and bring Xyl'Tharra to the brink of death
brief: The nest pulses like a heart, commander. Mechs, tripods, greys without end. And somewhere in there something very big is sleeping.
Kkt. You have my burrow. You have seen my sky. Come closer, little beings, and the mother awakens.
{leader} here. She heals on her ground, she broods, she screams. So we strike together, all at once. When the Swarm Mother falls, the swarm falls.
m11.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} followed you through the portal. On this world every human is an ally.
m11.won: Xyl'Tharra collapses, and above her space tears open: a rift, violet and black, with a sickly green-gold edge. It tears through both worlds and sucks everything in: our troops, the Zyrr with their mother, and back on Earth whole NEXUS columns and the cult's pilgrim trains. Then silence. We lie in red sand, above us a dusty sky with two tiny moons.
m11.lost: The Swarm Mother lives. Her scream echoes through the portal, and the swarm grows.

alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} followed you through the portal. On this world every human is a brother in faith.

m12.title: Stranded
m12.tagline: Scattered across the red desert: find a Verdan outpost and found a base
brief: Commander, we are alive! But the squads lie scattered in the red sand, far apart. No radio mast, no city. Only dunes, mesas and the bones of animals as big as houses. And a dust storm is coming.
Kkt ... Mother? Mother is silent. The rift ate us and spat us out here. No matter. The swarm builds a new nest, and you are the food.
KERN-0: LOCATION UNKNOWN. SUN TOO SMALL. TWO MOONS. RECALCULATING ... OBJECTIVE UNCHANGED: THE ARTIFACT.
You see? This is the Final Hour! The world has already burned, and we are its ashes. Brothers, sisters, take whatever still stands.

{leader} here. The scouts have spotted a ruin with red and white wings, a Verdan outpost, abandoned for generations. Gather there and take it, that will be our base. Then three more outposts, before the others contest the sand.
m12.won: The outpost is ours. Above the gate the Verdan emblem still hangs, red and white, with wings. What were they looking for here?
m12.lost: The sand has swallowed us. One day someone will find our helmets among the giant bones.

korvat.won: The outpost belongs to the people. Brodnik has already worked out how many fields fit into this desert.

m13.title: Ruins of the Forgotten
m13.tagline: Decipher three ruin sites and find out where the artifact lies
brief: Ruins stand everywhere in the sand: broken pillars, collapsed domes, half-buried statues with wings. The same runes as in the old empire depots. Commander, this was Verdan.
Kkt. Stone heaps of dead beings. The swarm smells something beneath, something old. We dig first.
KERN-0: VERDAN SCRIPT DETECTED. THE EMPIRE WAS HERE. THE EMPIRE IS ME. THE RUINS BELONG TO ME.

A Verdan guardian sleeps next to every site, a gun straight out of the legends. Whoever comes within three tiles of the site wakes it. Then it fires at whatever stands closest to the site. Keep a unit on a site for a whole round, then we can read the runes.
{leader} here. The Forgotten, those are the old Verdan. We want to know where they went and why. Decipher three sites, hold the headquarters. Then we will know where the artifact lies.
m13.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} is stranded too. We keep the guardians off your back, you read the runes.
m13.won: The runes speak: the Verdan built a machine against time, the artifact. In the Great Standstill they drained all the power of their empire, tore a gate into this world and hid it deep beneath the sand. Those who stayed behind forgot them. The trail leads to a canyon in the heart of the desert.
m13.lost: The ruins are silent. Others read the runes now, and all we understand is sand.

velkar.won: The runes are a formula: a machine against time, hidden in the Great Standstill deep beneath the sand. {leader} is already taking notes. The trail leads to a canyon in the heart of the desert.

m14.title: The Cave Entrance
m14.tagline: Hold the mouth in the canyon for three rounds, everyone wants in
brief: There it is, the canyon from the runes! At its end a mouth in the rock, as big as a cathedral, with the winged emblem above it. Cold air blows out of it. And the others have found it too.
Kkt. The hole leads down, to what we smell. The swarm descends first.
KERN-0: ACCESS TO THE ARTIFACT LOCATED. ALL OTHER UNITS: PLEASE STAND BACK.
A gate into the depths! The bell calls from below. Whoever climbs down there does not climb back up, except us.
{leader} here. We occupy the cave entrance for three rounds in a row, then we descend. And the headquarters does not fall, no matter who comes from where.
m14.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} seals off the canyon. You descend, we hold the position up here.
m14.won: The cave entrance is ours. We lower the ropes. Something glows down there, deep, deep beneath the red desert.
m14.lost: Others descend into the depths. Their cheers echo from the mouth, and then a light.

dravon.won: The cave entrance is secured. {leader} is the first to rope down. Something glows below, deep beneath the red desert.

alvenia.ally: {allyLeader} to {leader}: {ally} seals off the gorge. You climb down, your brothers in faith hold the line above.

campaign.intro: The sky burned: the Zyrr mothership lies in the desert, the bell tolls by itself, NEXUS has awakened, and the Zyrr are building a gate to their homeworld. Beyond it waits a third world that everyone has forgotten. Choose a human faction and hold the front, on three worlds.
campaign.chooseHint: Every human faction has its own run with its own progress. You can switch at any time.
campaign.migrated: Your previous campaign progress now continues as the {faction} run. The operations are new, unlocks and stars are kept.
campaign.replay: Replay the campaign with another human faction
campaign.replayHint: Time starts over. Who leads humanity this time?
twist: The runes flare up, the same runes as on the Verdan ruins. {leader} lays a hand on the artifact. The light swallows everything ...
... and the bell strikes again. Somewhere in Earth's desert a mothership crashes into the sand, and in its belly a violet gate flickers. The red world lies empty and forgotten as before.
The Starfall. As if nothing had happened. That is what the Verdan built the artifact for: whoever touches it turns back time. Xyl'Tharra breathes again, and everything begins anew.
campaign.persuadeTip: Tip: as {faction} you can persuade neutral settlements instead of conquering them. One unit next to it, from {cost} stars, no shot fired.

pitch.korvat: Mass, march, mettle: cheap infantry in droves. For everyone who brings a lot of boots.
pitch.dravon: Drill and veterans: every unit gets tougher. For everyone who strikes with precision.
pitch.alvenia: Faith and long-range arms: often with brothers in faith at its side, wins settlements by sermon instead of storm. Holds every position and judges the sinners.
pitch.meridon: Trade and harbours: plenty of stars, buys settlements instead of storming them. Gets help more often.
pitch.velkar: Production and fortresses: faster to new technology. For everyone who calculates before shooting.

epilogue.korvat: The League has held. The furrows become fields again, and the songs are about us.
epilogue.dravon: Discipline has beaten the stars. No recruit will ever forget this day.
epilogue.alvenia: We won because our brothers in faith stood at our side. Today every bell of the Order rings.
epilogue.meridon: The artifact is ours. Priceless. I already have three offers anyway.
epilogue.velkar: The formula is proven. Endless energy lies ahead. Please do not touch anything.

a1.title: World I: Earth
a1.tagline: Starfall, Bell, Awakening, Portal: the factions fight for Earth
a1.closing: World I: Earth holds. The cult is silent, NEXUS is pushed back, and the Zyrr portal stands open. We went through.

a2.title: World II: Zyrr Homeworld
a2.tagline: Violet sky, two moons, the nest of the Swarm Mother
a2.closing: World II: Xyl'Tharra lay at death's door when space tore open. The rift swallowed everyone, friend and foe, and spat them out into a red desert.

a3.title: World III: World of the Forgotten
a3.tagline: Red desert, Verdan ruins, everyone against everyone for the artifact
a3.closing: World III: The artifact of the Forgotten is in the hands of {faction}. The red desert is silent. For one breath.

campaign.expanded: The campaign has grown: the portal, the Zyrr homeworld and the world of the Forgotten are waiting. The old defensive battle now lives in operation 2. Stars and unlocks are kept.
campaign.landing: Landing party without a city: capture the outpost, or there will be no reinforcements.
campaign.bossEmerge: {name} has appeared! The Swarm Mother defends her nest.
campaign.bossLine: Kkt. You crawled through my gate, {leader}. Now you see me. It will be the last thing you see.
campaign.bossBrood: The Swarm Mother broods: {n} new greys!
campaign.reordered: The campaign now spans three worlds: first Earth, then the Zyrr homeworld, finally the red desert of the Forgotten. The portal is now the last operation on Earth, followed by three new operations in the desert. Won operations stay open, stars are kept, and you continue with the first open operation.
campaign.landingDesert: Stranded without a city: take the Verdan outpost, or there will be no reinforcements.
campaign.landingBurrow: Landing party without a base: capture the Zyrr burrow, or there will be no reinforcements.
campaign.towerTip: One more thing, commander: there are transmitter towers on the map. Capture them, reinforcements arrive there. They train troops but do not grow.
campaign.towerHoldTip: One more thing, commander: the transmitter towers train troops but do not grow. The count happens at the start of your turn. If a tower falls, the count starts over.
campaign.plansSeized: War plans seized! Bring the carrier to the HQ.
campaign.plansDropped: The carrier has fallen. The war plans lie on the ground!
campaign.plansReturned: The Fanatics took the war plans back to the temple.
campaign.plansLine: Thieves in the temple! Brothers, sisters, bring me back the plans, and the thief with them!
campaign.plansTip: Tip: only land units right next to the temple can seize the plans. Send a fast jeep with an escort. Once the plans are gone, the cult sends pursuers every {n} rounds.

weather.rainDesc: Artillery and Sun Lance range -1, helicopter and octocopter movement -1; with hit luck, more misses and grazes
weather.snowDesc: All vehicles (walkers and mechs too) move 1 tile less, at least 1; with hit luck, more misses (aliens freeze most)
weather.windDesc: Helicopters burn {windFuel} fuel per round; with hit luck, ranged units and flyers miss more often
weather.setupHint: Changes every {weatherCycle} rounds. Rain, snow and wind slow certain units and, with hit luck, raise the miss chance (wind only for ranged units and flyers, robots barely).
weather.dustDesc: Vision 1 tile less, units with range 2 or more lose 1 range, helicopters move 1 tile less; with hit luck, clearly more misses
weather.meteorDesc: At the start of each round 1 to 2 damage to every unarmoured unit (foot troops) outside cities and bunkers, never lethal
weather.acidDesc: At the start of each round 1 to 2 damage to every unit that is not Zyrr, outside cities and bunkers, never lethal; with hit luck more misses and grazes, as in rain
weather.quakeDesc: Only foot troops can move this round, vehicles, walkers, flyers and ships stand still; attacks and Verdan guns carry on
weather.calmDesc: The cavern is calm, no effects

select: The harvest waits, so does the enemy.
corpse: Poor fellow. Who ploughs his field now?
Bones in the field. Bad sign.
wreck: Scrap! We will melt it into tractors.
That used to be a proud vehicle.
forest: All alone in the woods ... comrades?
Something is creaking in the undergrowth.
Without the collective the forest is so quiet.
idle: My helmet is too big. As always.
rain: Rain is good for grain, bad for socks.
snow: Cold as the field kitchen in winter.

corpse: Do not stop, that is an order.
wreck: That thing has resigned from service.
forest: Trees. Grown without discipline.
Alone in the woods. No orders for this.
Who authorised this forest?
idle: I do not smile behind the visor.
rain: Rain is no excuse for weakness!
snow: Snow? Orders are not to freeze!

select: The light is with us, go!
move: The sun halo shows the way!
Step by step, prayer by prayer.
attack: In the name of the light!
kill: May the light be merciful to you.
hurt: I bleed, but I do not yield!
corpse: May he rest in the light.
We carry your light onward, brother.
wreck: The wreck gives cover. Thank the heavens!
forest: All alone ... just me and the light.
The forest is silent. I pray quietly.
Hello? Anyone from the Order here?
idle: I would like a short prayer.
I am polishing the sun halo.
rain: Wet visor, all I see is light.
snow: Snow! The light keeps us warm.

select: Time is money, what is up?
What is in it for me?
corpse: No more returns for that one.
wreck: Scrap metal! What does it fetch per ton?
forest: No sea, no market, only trees ...
Nobody hears me haggle out here.
Alone in the woods. Bad deal.
rain: Rain! Umbrellas at a special price!

wreck: Wreck provides 1 point of cover. Acceptable.
forest: Signal strength low. Alone.
Tree density high, visibility low.
No network in the woods.
snow: Outside temperature below zero. As planned.

forest: Too much green. Must terraform.
Trees. They stare back.
Alone in the chlorophyll ...
idle: When will this planet finally be violet?

move: Every step brings the end closer.
forest: The trees whisper of the end.
Alone in the woods ... I hear voices.
Firewood for the great day.
idle: When does the world finally end?
I already moved the date three times.

forest: High humidity. Rust risk.
Alone in the woods. No signal.
Trees: unoptimised structures.
idle: Does anyone have the wifi password?

briefing: Comrade Commander, fields are sown, troops are fed. Now we harvest land!
The collective is watching you. Not one step back, and nobody left behind.
I drove a tractor, you lead armies. Together we plough this map.
contact: Ah, {faction}! Come to our table. Those who share bread shoot less often.
{leader}, I am Brodnik. We are many, we are patient. Remember that.
Greetings, {faction}. Our steppe is wide, but our eyes reach further.
break: {leader}, our patience has been harvested. Peace ends next round!
The collective has voted: unanimously against you, {faction}.
I offered you my hand. Now I offer you my fist.
war: War it is! Every plough becomes a tank, every scythe a banner!
{faction}, you have woken the farmer. You will regret it by harvest.
Everyone to the fields! Today we do not sow, today we march!
peaceOffer: {leader}, enough trenches dug. Let us plant potatoes instead.
The collective is tired, and you do not look fresh either. Peace?
I offer peace. Once. A farmer does not like to repeat himself.
peaceAccepted: Wise choice, {leader}. Brodnik never forgets friends. Nor enemies.
Peace! Tonight there is soup for everyone, even for {faction}.
You see? Together is easier. I always tell my children the same.
peaceRejected: You refuse my hand? Then you will soon feel my boot, {leader}!
Refused?! The collective will remember. The collective remembers everything.
Fine. Then we plough straight through you, {faction}.
cityLost: {city} belongs to the people! We take it back, house by house!
You take {city} from us? Our grandmothers will chase you with ladles!
A setback, not an end. The collective does not yield, {leader}!
cityTaken: {city} is a cooperative now. The people even get breakfast.
Thanks for {city}, {leader}. We ploughed the fields right away.
You see, {faction}? Many small steps, and suddenly the city is ours.
eliminated: Impossible... the collective... who will feed the chickens now?
I am going back to my tractor. It never betrayed me.
The steppe was too wide, the harvest too short. Farewell, comrades.
grandProject: {project} stands! Built by a thousand hands, paid for with zero grumbling.
Look, {leader}: {project}. That is what happens when everyone pitches in.
The people have raised {project}. And tomorrow they will raise more.
victory: Victory! Tonight the choir sings, and tomorrow we sow again.
I knew it, Commander. One people, one step, one victory!
The map belongs to the collective. Now everyone to the harvest festival!
defeat: Lost? But we ploughed everything so neatly...
The collective is beaten. I need to sit down for a moment.
So many fields, so little luck. Next time we sow earlier, comrade.

briefing: Briefing. Short. Target: everything. Mistakes: none. Dismissed.
Commander. Barracks full, boots polished. Execute.
I expect discipline. Not luck. Luck is for civilians.
contact: {faction}. Logged. Classified. Observed.
Voss speaking. You are in my files now, {leader}.
Contact established. Stay behind your line, {faction}.
break: Treaty terminated. Notice: one round. Use it to pray.
{leader}. The peace was a drill. The drill is over.
New orders for {faction}: none. For my troops: many.
war: War. Finally an honest condition.
Target marked: {faction}. Weapons free.
You wanted this, {leader}. I always did.
peaceOffer: Ceasefire. Offer stands one round. No negotiation.
{leader}. My men need drill, not graves. Peace?
Tactical pause offered. Do not mistake it for friendship.
peaceAccepted: Signed. I measured your borders anyway.
Peace with {faction}. For now. Everything is for now.
Sensible, {leader}. Sense suits you. Keep it.
peaceRejected: Refused. Noted. You will regret that note.
No peace? Good. I hate paperwork anyway.
{leader}, that was your last mistake. The list is long.
cityLost: {city} lost. So is its garrison chief.
You have {city}. For now. I have your address, {leader}.
Unacceptable. Counterattack in preparation. Thorough.
cityTaken: {city} secured. Curfew effective immediately.
Your city, {leader}? Now a barracks. Nice windows.
{city} has fallen. Precise. Punctual. As planned.
eliminated: Imposs... retreat... no. No retreat. Only... the end.
Write it down: Voss did not flinch. Only the mask did.
The barracks are empty. Lights out. Dismissed.
grandProject: {project} completed. On schedule. Naturally.
See {project}, {leader}? That is discipline in concrete.
{project} stands. Guarded. Around the clock.
victory: Victory. Expected. Roll call at five tomorrow.
Mission accomplished, Commander. I am smiling. You just cannot see it.
The map is in order. Finally.
defeat: Defeat? That is... not in the regulations.
Impossible. I demand a rematch. Immediately.
The mask stays on. So no one sees what happens beneath it.

briefing: Welcome, Commander. The Order has prayed: we win, but without sin.
Our Light Wardens stand ready, our Sun Lances too. Choose wisely.
A short sermon, I promise: hold, judge, redeem. Go.
contact: Greetings, {leader}. I am Liora Valen, High Priestess. Are you without sin?
Welcome, {faction}. The light sees everything, you too.
Delighted, {leader}. May our path be a peaceful one.
break: With regret, {leader}: the Order revokes the peace. The clock is running.
I prayed and hesitated. The light has decided.
You have exhausted our patience, {faction}. The Judgement approaches.
war: War. I hate that word. But the light demands it.
{leader}, you leave me no choice. Light Wardens, forward.
The Order defends itself. Patiently, thoroughly and without mercy for sinners.
peaceOffer: {leader}, the bells ring for peace. Do you hear them?
An offer from the Order: peace. Sincerely meant, sworn before the light.
Enough fallen on both sides. Let us lower our weapons.
peaceAccepted: Blessed be you, {leader}. Reason is a virtue.
Peace with {faction}. The Order sings a hymn of thanks. Even the novices.
Sealed before the light. Do not break it, that would be a sin.
peaceRejected: Refused? Then the hard way. The Order knows that one too, {leader}.
I am entering your refusal into the book of sins. In golden ink.
A pity, {faction}. My patience was great. Was.
cityLost: {city}? But that was home to our finest chapel!
That is sacrilege, {leader}! The Judgement will find you!
We have lost {city}. I need a prayer, please, right now.
cityTaken: {city} now stands beneath the sun halo. May the light heal here.
Do not worry, {leader}: {city} now has prayers. And hospitals.
We now keep {city} in the name of the Order. Very faithfully. For a very long time.
eliminated: This ... this was not foretold. I pray for forgiveness.
The Order falls? Please ... someone must carry the light onward.
I was a doctor. I know when it is over. May the light redeem us.
grandProject: The Order consecrates {project}. With bells, incense and a very long sermon.
{project} is complete, {leader}. Built with faith. You were not invited.
A monument to the light: {project}. Feel free to admire it, humbly.
victory: Victory! The light has won, and no sin went unjudged.
The Order has prayed as one: you are splendid, Commander.
We won. Now everyone change your bandages, and then we celebrate.
defeat: Lost? That cannot be. Did the light ... blink?
All the prayers, all the vows ... and still. I am speechless. Almost.
Please tell the Order that I ... need a moment of silence.

briefing: Commander, the dice are cast, the vaults are full. Let us play high.
Every harbour has its price. Find it, I pay cash.
My stake: everything. Your job: make sure I do not regret it, darling.
contact: {leader}! A new customer. I have already worked out your price.
Ahoy, {faction}. My spies knew you before you knew yourself.
Welcome to the table, {leader}. The house always wins. I am the house.
break: Our contract expires, {leader}. No renewal, no refund.
I am cancelling the peace. Doing business with you did not pay off.
The stock of {faction} is falling. I am selling. With cannons.
war: War is just another market, {leader}. And I am buying your coasts.
All hands to the guns! We are collecting a debt.
I bet it all on red. Your red, {faction}. Figuratively speaking.
peaceOffer: {leader}, war is bad for business. Peace? I will add interest.
An offer you can hardly refuse: peace at a friendly price.
Cards on the table: peace, and nobody loses their last shirt.
peaceAccepted: Deal! The handshake counts. You can read the fine print later.
Peace with {faction}. My merchants are already at your border.
A good deal, {leader}. Mostly for me.
peaceRejected: You turn down my offer? That will cost you, {leader}. Dearly.
Refused? Then I raise the stakes. And you pay.
Bad hand, {faction}. You should have folded.
cityLost: {city}? That was my best harbour! Who pays me back now?
A city lost, {leader}? No, only lent. At loan-shark rates.
My spy did not report this. My spy is fired.
cityTaken: {city} changes hands. I call it a hostile takeover.
Thanks for {city}, {leader}. Harbour fees go to me from now on.
{city} is bought. I paid with your mistakes.
eliminated: Bankrupt? Me? That... that must be a calculation error.
I bet on the wrong horse. For the first time. And the last.
Tell my creditors... no, better tell them nothing.
grandProject: {project} is finished. Admission for {faction}: double.
Admire {project}, {leader}. Built with your money, indirectly.
My new showpiece: {project}. I won it at cards.
victory: Jackpot! I knew you were a good hand, Commander.
The bank wins. As always. Bubbly for the whole fleet!
Bet everything, won everything. I love this game.
defeat: Lost? Me? No, no, the game was rigged!
My fortune... my fleet... my hair! All gone.
That was not a loss, Commander. Just a very expensive lesson.

briefing: Hypothesis: we win. Experimental setup: you. Begin the experiment.
Commander, the labs are humming, the formulas check out. Touch nothing.
I have calculated everything. Except you. You are the variable.
contact: Fascinating! A new species: {faction}. May I take samples?
{leader}, Director Kesh here. Your behaviour is now being logged.
New data point: {faction}. I shall call it Specimen B for now.
break: Peace trial concluded. Result: boring. War next round.
{leader}, your readings are abnormal. I must abort the experiment.
The formula says war. I never contradict the formula.
war: War! Finally, field trials under real conditions!
{faction}, you are now officially a test subject. Congratulations.
Cold, precision, superiority. Three words, one problem for you, {leader}.
peaceOffer: {leader}, my statistics recommend peace. Do follow the statistics.
The war disturbs my measurements. Peace? Purely scientific, of course.
Offer: ceasefire. Probability of your acceptance: 61.3 percent.
peaceAccepted: As predicted. I love being right, {leader}.
Peace with {faction}. Deviation from the model: zero point zero.
Excellent. Now I can go back to blowing things up in peace.
peaceRejected: Refused? That contradicts my data! Then I shall correct you instead.
Illogical, {leader}. And illogic gets frozen in my laboratory.
Interesting. Wrong, but interesting. Note: specimen is unreasonable.
cityLost: {city}?! My blueprints were there! Thirty years of development!
That was not in the model! Who deleted {city} from the model?
Error in the experimental setup. I... I need to recalculate.
cityTaken: {city} becomes a test works. The residents may help count.
Thanks for {city}, {leader}. Your mistake was statistically predictable.
Experiment successful: {city} acquired. Please applaud quietly.
eliminated: Result... negative. I... would have liked to know that earlier.
All data lost. Please... someone switch off the cooling.
I was so close. Just one more formula. Just one more...
grandProject: {project} is operational! Side effects: negligible. Mostly.
Do you see {project}, {leader}? No? It is not meant for laymen.
Breakthrough! {project} is running. I only lost two assistants.
victory: Victory. Exactly as calculated. Well, I adjusted the formula a bit.
Experiment successful! Commander, you get your own lab coat.
Who calculates, wins. I calculated. We won.
defeat: Defeat? That... that is statistically almost impossible!
My formula was perfect. So it must have been yours, Commander.
I... I need more data. And a very strong coffee.

briefing: Kkt. Commander-unit, listen you. This planet becomes violet. Begin.
Swarm is ready. Saucers are polished. Primitives are clueless. Zrrk.
We do not land. We stay. Terraform, conquer, then snack. Kkt.
contact: Kkt. New lifeform: {faction}. Small. Soft. Cute.
We greet you, {leader}-being. You have so few eyes. Sad.
Zrrk! {faction} discovered. Is tagged as: later.
break: Peace-phase ended. Swarm hungers for your land, {leader}.
Kkt. Treaty is dissolved. In acid. Next round.
We have thought, {faction}. With all brains. Answer: no.
war: War! Warm up death rays. Kkt. Kkt. Kkt.
{faction} becomes violet. Whether {faction} wants or not. Zrrk.
You woke the swarm, {leader}. Swarm is grumpy.
peaceOffer: Kkt. Swarm offers pause. Not from pity. From curiosity.
{leader}-being, we not ray you for a while. Accept?
Peace is strange concept. We want to try. Zrrk?
peaceAccepted: Kkt! Peace. We watch you anyway. With all eyes.
Good, {leader}-being. You may stay non-violet a while longer.
Zrrk. {faction} now has pet status. Very honourable.
peaceRejected: Refused?! Kkt kkt KKT! Swarm is offended!
{leader}-being says no. Swarm says: ray.
We offered pause. You choose radiation. Zrrk. Strange choice.
cityLost: Kkt?! {city} gone? But ground was already so nicely violet!
Primitives take our nest? That... not in plan. Zrrk.
Swarm is confused. Swarm counts again. Swarm is less.
cityTaken: {city} is now nest. We paint everything violet. Kkt.
Thanks for {city}, {leader}-being. Very cosy. Bit too little acid.
Zrrk. {city} collected. For the collection.
eliminated: Kkt... mothership... calls... we... come... home...
Swarm goes quiet. Too quiet. Zrrk... zrk... z.
This planet... will not be violet. Only a little. Back there.
grandProject: {project} complete. Primitives marvel. Good. Kkt.
Look, {leader}-being: {project}. We built it with thoughts.
Zrrk! {project} hums. Soon everything hums. Violet.
victory: Kkt! Planet is violet. Swarm is pleased. Snack for everyone.
Commander-unit did well. You may have one extra eye.
Zrrk zrrk! New home secured. Mothership will be so proud.
defeat: Kkt?! Primitives win? That... is not possible in this galaxy.
Swarm loses. Swarm must... rethink. With all brains.
Zrrk... we pack saucers. Planet was too green anyway.

briefing: The bell tolls, Chosen One. The final hour begins with your first move.
It is written: we need no cities. Only fire and faith. Go.
The embers whisper your name, Commander. Do not keep them waiting.
contact: Ah, {faction}. The prophecy mentioned you. In a footnote.
Welcome, {leader}. I have already seen your end. It was lovely.
The bell knows you already, {faction}. It just has not rung yet.
break: The embers have spoken, {leader}: peace burns away in one round.
Repent, {faction}. You have exactly one turn left to do so.
The writing on the wall is clear. I wrote it myself.
war: The hour has come! Ring the bells, light the torches!
{faction}, the ashes are calling you. And ashes are very patient.
It is written, {leader}: you burn. Chapter three, verse eight.
peaceOffer: The prophecy permits a pause. A short one. Use it to repent.
{leader}, even fire must draw breath. Peace, until the bell tolls?
I offer mercy. That rarely happens. The stars are mild today.
peaceAccepted: Wise, {leader}. The bell falls silent. For now. It has a good memory.
Peace with {faction}, as foretold. Everything is foretold.
Good. I shall pray for you. Loudly. With torches.
peaceRejected: You spurn mercy? Then receive the embers, {leader}!
Refused? The prophecy feared this. And rejoiced.
{faction} chooses fire. The fire gratefully accepts.
cityLost: You desecrate {city}? May your soup be cold forever!
Take {city}, {leader}. Ashes cannot be held.
Sacrilege! The bell tolls for you, {faction}. Loudly. And off-key.
cityTaken: {city} has made an offering. Generously. Under some pressure.
Thanks for the treasures of {city}, {leader}. We left the bells.
It was written: {city} shall be plundered. Page twelve, top left.
eliminated: The bell... tolls... for me? That was not in the text...
The final hour has come. Only, sadly, mine.
The embers die. But ashes... travel far. Remember that.
grandProject: {project} is complete. A sign! I ordered it myself.
Behold, {leader}: {project}. Kneeling before it will soon be mandatory.
The bell tolls for {project}. And right afterwards for you.
victory: It is done! The prophecy was right. As always. Almost always.
The final hour struck for everyone else. For us, the festival bells ring.
Commander, the embers are pleased. A rare thing. Enjoy it.
defeat: That... was not foretold. Who read the scroll upside down?
The bell is silent. The torches smoke. I am... shaken.
Impossible! The stars were favourable! I shall sue the stars!

hit.title: Hit luck
hit.setupHint: Attacks can miss, graze, partly hit or land a critical hit ({hitMin} to {hitMax} % damage). Weather and race change the odds.

raceDesc.alien: Many critical hits but also many misses; snow makes them even less accurate.
raceDesc.robot: Almost always full hits, hardly any misses or crits; weather barely matters.
raceDesc.cult: Often critical, often off target: fanatic and unpredictable.

hit.hintLuck: Hit luck: the result ranges from a miss to a critical hit.

unitDesc.teslaTank: Own hit odds: often misses ({miss} %), but attack {atk} instead of the tank's {base}; critical hits remain possible ({crit} %).
unitDesc.railSniper: Own hit odds: machine precision, only {miss} % misses and {crit} % critical hits.

hit.unitRule: Own hit odds of single units:

factionCritDesc.dravon: Dravon's drill pays off: all Dravon units land a critical hit (one and a half times the damage) in {pct} % instead of {base} % of attacks; the extra critical hits come out of the full hits. Weather works as for all humans.

retreat.desc: Fires with {retreatPct} % damage without return fire and falls back one tile. Then a {retreatCooldown}-round cooldown.

rear.name: Attack from behind
rear.rule: Every unit faces one of eight directions: the direction of its last step; an attacker turns towards its target, a unit returning fire towards the attacker. New units face the map centre. If the attacker stands in the target's rear (the three tiles behind it, the same cone at range), it deals {pct} % more damage, before hit luck. Flanks do not count, nor does return fire. Structures, wonders and guns have no rear. An arrow on the base shows the facing of the selected unit.

moveFire.tagDesc: This unit has already moved this turn. If it attacks now, it deals only {pct} % damage, then hit luck applies. The target's return fire stays unchanged.

bonusDesc.korvat: After moving, all Korvat units attack with {pct} % instead of {base} % damage, Steppe Riders even with {rider} %. Hit luck still applies.
bonusDesc.dravon: Dravon's soldiers are the best trained: after moving, all Dravon units attack with {pct} % instead of {base} % damage. Hit luck still applies.

homeDefense.tagDesc: Stands on own territory: +{pct} % defence when this unit is attacked. Does not apply when it attacks, nor to return fire.

bonusDesc.alvenia: All Alvenia units defend with +{pct} % on their own territory, on top of city, terrain and cover. Only when they are attacked, not when they attack and not for return fire.

memorial.name: Memorial
memorial.desc: When a soldier (foot troop of any faction, the cult's own included) dies on land outside a city, the cult puts the corpse on display: the tile becomes a memorial for this and {rounds} more rounds, a new death there refreshes the duration. Attacking from the memorial: cult fanatics deal +{zeal} % damage, human attackers -{fear} % (fear). Robots and aliens know no fear. Applies to the own attack only, not to return fire.
memorial.tile: Cult memorial ({unit}), {n} more rounds: fanatics attack from here with +{zeal} %, human attackers with -{fear} % (fear)
memorial.zealDesc: Stands on a cult memorial: +{pct} % damage on its own attack, {n} more rounds. Does not apply to return fire.
memorial.fearDesc: Stands on a cult memorial: fear, -{pct} % damage on its own attack, {n} more rounds. Does not apply to return fire.

repair.desc: Salvages a wreck on or next to the tile: double the normal healing, the unit does not fight this round. The wreck is used up.

rockets.desc: Ranged attack two tiles away. Reload only in an own city with a depot (at turn start).

cover.ranged: Cover against ranged attacks: ×1.4 defence against attacks from 2+ tiles (ground troops and vehicles)

victory.title: Victory tracker
victory.hint: Every faction has its own victory condition. Factions without contact stay hidden.
victory.off: Faction victory is off in this game.
victory.setupHint: Each faction can also win through its own victory condition (its own tier-3 victory tech).
victory.researchOnly: Your faction does not research otherwise. Only the victory tech can be researched.
victory.ruleInterrupt: Attacks reset the current phase to 0; finished phases are kept.
victory.ruleNoInterrupt: Attacks do not interrupt it, but the structure can be destroyed.
victory.ruleDrill: Moving and attacks reset the counter to 0.
victory.ruleWaal: Fires from the second phase on (range {r}), never moves.

goal.korvat: Own more than {pct} % of all cities on the map (villages count). Victory at the start of your turn.
goal.dravon: Build the land cruiser Waal on free land in your territory. After {arm} rounds it fires (range {range}), after {total} rounds it is finished and you win. Attacks do not interrupt it, but it has few HP while building.
goal.alvenia: Great Judgement: destroy {n} units of sinners ({min} to {max} by map size). Only kills after the Great Judgement is unlocked count. A sinner, for {rounds} rounds, is whoever plunders, burns, converts, captures a foreign city, breaks a peace or attacks Alvenia; aliens and robots are permanent sinners.
goal.meridon: Have {n} stars in the treasury. Victory at the start of your turn.
goal.velkar: Build the fusion power plant on 2x2 free land (mountains allowed) in your territory. After {n} rounds it delivers endless energy and you win. Every attack resets the progress to 0.
goal.zyrr: Build the dimensional portal in your territory: {build} rounds of construction, then {charge} rounds of charging. An attack resets the current phase to 0; finished construction is kept.
goal.vesper: A prophet calls up the earth-core drill onto an adjacent tile. If it stands still for {n} rounds in a row, it reaches the earth's core and the world ends. Moving and attacks reset the counter.
goal.nexus: Build the hacker relay on a mountain in your territory or with an own outpost: {build} rounds of construction, then {hack} rounds of hacking. An attack resets the current phase to 0; finished construction is kept.
goal.meridonAny: Have {n} stars in the treasury in points games ({m} in games without a round limit). Victory at the start of your turn.
