onboarding.title: Play the tutorial?
onboarding.text: Your first operation. In a few turns the tutorial covers the goal, moving, capturing, research, building, training, upkeep and combat.
onboarding.playDesc: A short practice game against an easy AI. You can quit at any time.
onboarding.later: You can find the tutorial and the rules in the main menu at any time.

rules.title: Rules
rules.intro: The essentials in brief. Tap a section to expand or collapse it.

goal.title: Goal & game modes
goal.text: Points mode: after {rounds} rounds the highest score wins (medal at the top). Points come from explored tiles ({tile}), territory tiles ({territory}), city levels ({level}), techs ({tech} per tier) and more. Conquest: the last side holding cities wins. Endless and sandbox have no round limit. Faction victories (optional): every faction can also win through its own goal. The victory tracker in the menu shows the standings.

turn.title: Round & stars
turn.text: All factions take turns one after another; a round ends when everyone has moved. At the start of your turn stars come in: {city} per city level, {hq} extra for the headquarters, plus bonuses from buildings, rewards and embassies. Stars are the only currency for units, buildings, research and upgrades. You start with {start} stars.

upkeep.title: Upkeep
upkeep.text: The first {free} units are core troops and pay no upkeep. Every further unit costs {pct} % of its price per round (rounded up), tanks a flat {tank}. Korvat pays {korvat} % less upkeep (applied to the total, rounded up). Upkeep is deducted from income. Next to the stars at the top you see the net income per round, the unit panel shows each unit's upkeep.

combat.title: Combat & hit luck
combat.text: Select a unit, then an enemy in range. The attack button shows the preview: expected damage with its range, such as “≈4 damage (0–6)”, the kill chance and the return fire. A surviving defender strikes back if it can reach the attacker. Tanks drive {tankMove} tiles and fire {tankRange} tiles, but strike back only at {tankReturn} tile. Hit luck (optional) sets the damage: miss {miss} %, graze {graze} %, partial hit {partial} %, full hit {full} %, critical {crit} %. Every race has its own odds and the weather shifts them. Counter units deal more damage to certain classes. Firing after moving: a unit that first moves and then attacks in the same turn deals only {move} % damage, and only then is hit luck rolled. This applies to melee, ranged attacks, rockets, guns and splash damage. A unit that stands still fires at full strength, and the defender's return fire stays unchanged.

cover.title: Cover
cover.text: Units with “Garrison” defend ×{city} in own cities, ×{bunker} with a {ring}. Infantry, MG, snipers and pioneers (Light Wardens and railgun marksmen too) defend ×{outpost} on an own outpost. With the matching research, forests, mountains and (for ships) coasts defend ×{terrain}. Troops and tanks in forests or cities also defend ×{ranged} against ranged attacks from two or more tiles. Fliers get no cover. The tile panel shows the cover.

abilities.title: Abilities (retreat, repair, rockets)
abilities.text: Orderly retreat (human ground troops): fires with {retreat} % damage without return fire and falls back one tile, then locked for {cooldown} rounds; after a move in the same turn this shot is reduced to {move} % as well, the step back does not count for it. Emergency repair (robots): salvages a wreck on or next to the tile and heals {repair} % of normal healing; the unit does not fight this round. Rockets (mechs): ranged attack on targets exactly {range} tiles away, {max} rockets, reloaded at turn start in an own city with a {depot}.

cities.title: Cities & research
cities.text: Move a unit onto a settlement or enemy city; at the start of your next turn you can capture it. Buildings on resources in the city area add population, a full population raises the city level: more income, more units and a reward. With every level the city territory grows by up to {grow} free tiles in the next ring, nearest first, up to at most {max} x {max} tiles; foreign territory stays foreign. Transmitter towers (in the campaign; in free games bases stand there) are neutral places: they train troops and bring {towerInc} stars per round, but do not grow. Every city has {slots} slots for upgrades. Every upgrade also raises the unit limit by {cap}. Buy level: for {buy} × (level + 1) stars a city rises one level at once (level 1 → 2: {ex2}, 2 → 3: {ex3}, 3 → 4: {ex4}), with the usual reward; once per city and round, not for transmitter towers, supply lines or the cult. Research unlocks units, buildings and upgrades and gets dearer with every city: tier 1 costs {t1} stars with one city, {t1c3} with three cities, tier 3 costs {t3c3} with three cities. The tile panel shows locked buildings with “Requires: …”.

outposts.title: Outposts
outposts.text: With {tech}, infantry, MG, snipers and pioneers (Light Wardens and railgun marksmen too) build an outpost on their tile for {cost} stars and defend ×{def} on it. If it borders own territory, the nearest city gains the free tiles around it. Two outposts are always at least {outpostSpacing} tiles apart, even those of different factions. Enemies can capture outposts. Pioneers also build tank barriers ({barrier} stars) that slow vehicles.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy
diplomacy.text: Factions you have not met stay hidden. After the first contact you are at war. You can offer peace, the other side accepts or declines. Breaking a peace is announced one round in advance. With {tech} and a discovered headquarters you open embassies (the first costs {cost} stars, each further one {step} more); each gives both sides {income} stars per round.

factions.title: Faction victories
factions.text: Can be switched off in the setup. It needs the faction's own victory tech (tier 3), drawn with a dashed rim in the research. The victory tracker in the menu shows the progress of all known factions.

rules.productionNote: Human factions call this doctrines: they adopt doctrines that bring advantages, and their units come from production sites. The Zyrr, NEXUS and the cult research. Costs are the same.

emplacements.title: Gun emplacements (Dravon)
emplacements.text: Fortress building: with {tech}, Dravon pioneer squads and mine layers build a gun emplacement for {cost} stars on a free adjacent tile in own territory (passable land without a city, building, resource, feature or unit). At most {per} per own city, at least {spacing} tiles apart. The emplacement is a structure, not a unit: armour {hp}, attack {atk}, defence {def}, impassable, no upkeep and no score. At the start of every round it fires once at a visible unit in range {range} that is at war with Dravon (never at peace, never at allies), always with full damage and hit luck. Enemies attack it like a Verdan gun; once destroyed, rubble remains and no kill is counted. If the territory is lost or Dravon is eliminated, it is razed.

cult.title: Cult: plunder & horde
cult.text: The Cult of the Final Hour plays differently: when it takes a village or city, it plunders it for {base} stars plus {level} per city level ({hq} more for a headquarters); the same city brings loot again only after {again} rounds, {half} % the second time, {quarter} % after that. Cult cities bring no income, do not grow and do not train. They only provide slots for the horde (level + 1, own headquarters +{hqSlots}, shrine +{shrine}), plus {cap} base slots. Zealots, torchbearers, rocket zealots, prophets and doom crawlers call up new units onto a free adjacent tile for stars (zealots and prophets also call up berserkers), then a cooldown of {cooldown} rounds; the prophet also calls up the earth-core drill. The cult pays no upkeep, the horde brings a tithe ({tithe} stars per unit, at most {titheMax} per round and {titheRival} per rival faction), every plundered star counts {score} points ({scoreDuel} in a duel, more the more rivals). If the cult has no unit left, it is eliminated and its cities turn neutral.

judgement.title: Sin and Judgement
judgement.text: While Holy Alvenia is in the game, every other faction that plunders, burns (burn attack), converts hostile units, captures a city of another faction, breaks a peace or attacks Alvenia is marked as a sinner for {rounds} rounds; every new deed refreshes the mark. Aliens and robots (Zyrr, NEXUS) are permanent sinners without a deed as godless creatures; the Cathedral of Light's penance tithe counts only sinners with a deed. Judgement: Alvenia's units deal +{pct} % damage to sinners, return fire included. Martyr's Blessing: when an Alvenia unit falls in battle, own adjacent units heal {heal} HP and defend with +{def} % for {bless} rounds. Bulwark of Faith: +{home} % defence on own territory. Great Judgement (victory condition): destroy {n} units of sinners (14 × 14 map, more or fewer by size) once the Great Judgement is unlocked.

sites.title: Production sites (humans)
sites.text: The five human factions train a unit only in a city whose territory holds the matching production site: one per city, buildable without a doctrine. Every headquarters, every base of the barracks kind and every transmitter tower has barracks built in, Korvat and Dravon have them in every own city, and Dravon's headquarters also has a motor pool. Whoever captures a city takes over its sites. The Zyrr, NEXUS and the cult train as before.

ships.title: Ships and shipyard
ships.text: Every city with water in its territory or right next to the city tile buys ships under “Troops”; they launch empty on a free water tile at the city (shallow first, ocean only with diving). The landing boat costs {boat} stars and needs no base: a land unit moves onto it from an adjacent tile, boards and is ferried across. An empty ship has hull HP ({hull} for the boat) and cannot go ashore; the empty boat does not attack. Warships cost their upgrade price: humans need {base} or {dock} in the city, the cult and NEXUS the matching research. The cult and NEXUS need {tech} for boats as for embarking; the Zyrr wade and have no ships. As before: at an own {base} a land unit becomes a landing boat for free, ships upgrade in own territory, and whoever moves ashore becomes the carried unit again.

doctrines.title: Doctrines (humans)
doctrines.text: In the doctrine tree the human factions unlock no units but advantages, buildings and upgrades. Cost: (tier x cities + 4) x 5 stars. New effects:

factionUnits.title: Faction designs
factionUnits.text: Some factions have their own units or their own way of training. The numbers are also shown in the faction profile.

shadowFleet.title: Shadow fleet (Meridon)
shadowFleet.text: Only the Shadow Commando and the Fog Cutter are camouflaged: enemies only see them once one of their units, cities or structures stands right next to them, and after an own attack or a sabotage until the next own turn. The radar sweep, recon drone and radio tower find them. Withdraw: after an own attack without moving first, a land unit falls back up to {withdraw} tiles and attacks no more afterwards. Instead of infantry the barracks train marines ({marineCost} stars, {marineHp} HP, attack {marineAtk}, defence {marineDef}); they are amphibious and may still attack in the same turn after landing. Meridon builds neither tanks nor artillery but rocket silos: pioneers build one for {cost} stars on a free adjacent tile in own territory, at most {per} per city and {max} in total, {spacing} tiles apart. Every silo builds one Guided Missile per turn ({missileCost} stars) on a free tile next to it; it belongs to the city in whose territory the silo stands. Independently the silo launches a rocket on command at an explored tile (or a tile inside a radar sweep) up to {range} tiles away: {dmg} damage to every unit in the 2×2 area of target tile, right, below and diagonal, own ones too; cities and buildings stay. The land tiles without a city then burn for {fire} rounds: at the start of every round each unit on them loses {burn} HP. Then {cd} rounds of reloading. The city reward "tank" brings {rewardMissiles} Guided Missiles; captured tank factories and gun works give Meridon stars instead of units, Guided Missiles only come from the silo. The Radar Truck shows all hostile units within radius {radius} for {rr} rounds, under the clouds too ({rcd} rounds pause). The Shadow Commando sabotages a hostile outpost, building or road on its own tile or next to it ({scd} rounds pause). In return Meridon land units deal {weak} % less damage; ships and the naval base cost {sea} % less.

bases.title: Bases
bases.text: In free games on the default world every neutral place is a base of one of {kinds} kinds, including where transmitter towers would otherwise stand. It is unguarded: whoever finds it captures it like any village and uses it from the next turn. Tap it to see what it gives you before you capture it. Once captured it behaves like a city: it grows, levels up and can be upgraded, and its property applies on top for as long as you hold it. Next to every headquarters lies a barracks, the same for everyone. The other kinds are dealt as a mix: in turn one each of production, power, supply and protection, and no kind appears twice while another one would still find a place; with NEXUS in the game there is at least one power kind if a place suits it. For the five human factions the barracks, tank factory, military airfield, gun works and naval base come with the matching production site built in. Zyrr, cult and NEXUS have no production sites: for them the matching units cost {pct} % less everywhere while they hold the base; a faction without a matching unit gets {gap} stars per round instead. Residential blocks and the supermarket train troops for nobody (at most a quarter of the places other than the home barracks): their slots support units you train in other, full cities. Bunker, field hospital and supply depot contain the city upgrade of the same name in a stronger form; it cannot be bought there again. Of a base's stars the cult receives {tribute} % as tribute.

unitIcons.title: Unit icons
unitIcons.text: Every unit carries its badge: on the left the icon of its role, next to it the hit points, after that a veteran's star. Same role, same icon, for every faction; the troop cards and the unit panel show the same icons.

academy.title: Floating academy (Velkar)
academy.text: Velkar's capital is a floating academy (in free games; the campaign keeps the old rules). Captured places become research posts: one tile, stars and vision, no training, no upgrades. Their territory passes to the academy, plus {pop} population (+{perLevel} per level of the place above 1), and each post supports {units} more units. Territory stays where it is, even when the academy moves. The academy trains {base} units per turn plus one per post (at most {max}), on the academy or free tiles next to it. Lift-off: after {lift} round it floats and moves {move} tiles per turn over any terrain; landing means terraforming: the academy reshapes the tile for {tf} round and lands at the start of its next turn; meanwhile it keeps floating (same attack rules), does not move and can cancel (the turn's tiles are then used up). Mountain, forest and shallow water become plain, desert, steppe, tundra, hills and swamp become grassland, and this stays after lift-off; deep ocean, volcanoes and fires do not. A resource is absorbed (+{tfPop} population), neutral buildings, ruins and features are levelled, and so is an adjacent neutral place (it vanishes, its territory passes to the academy, no reward). Nothing owned by a faction, no wonder, gun or landmark is ever levelled. Not in foreign territory, no foreign unit, no own building, at least {gap} tiles from every place with an owner; free surroundings within radius {claim} become territory. If the landing is no longer possible at the start of the turn, it keeps floating. From lift-off until landing, production rests; it trains again in the landing turn. While floating, only flyers, flak and tanks attack; without a shield every hit forces an emergency landing. Shield ({cost} stars): {hp} HP, absorbs attacks on the academy and units on its tile first, recharges {regen} HP per turn, once destroyed it can be rebuilt only after {rebuild} rounds; while it stands the academy cannot be captured. Beam relay ({beamer} stars) on a post: one unit per round from the academy to it, one round in transit, arrives ready; if the relay falls, the unit returns to the academy. If the academy is lost, the nearest post becomes the new academy at half the level. Neutron beam (built in): one shot every {every} turns at a visible hostile unit or hostile structure within {brange} tiles; a full hit deals {bdmg} damage, weaker ones less, a miss nothing (without hit luck always {bdmg}); no return fire, no cities; on the ground, floating and while terraforming, not in the lift-off round. Academy upgrades (two ways: typical army or a flying fortress that holds out and then attacks itself), one price per level, one level per turn and module, in the air too: shield boost ({sCosts} stars, per level +{sHp} HP and +{sRegen} recharge), defence missiles ({mCosts} stars, one interception per level between two own turns against flyers, mech rockets and silo rockets on the academy and its adjacent tiles, not against ground fire), armour ({aCosts} stars, hull with {aHp} HP per level, recharges {aRegen} per turn; only without a hull the emergency landing, on the ground only capturable without shield and hull), beam amplifier ({bCosts} stars, fires every turn). Upgrades and beam are lost with the academy.

hacking.title: Hacking (NEXUS)
hacking.text: NEXUS hacks without units, only in free games. Remote takeover: tap a revealed neutral place (village, base, transmitter tower) and choose Hack. It becomes NEXUS territory as if a unit had captured it. Every data centre in NEXUS territory gives one hack charge, which recharges {recharge} rounds after a hack. A hack costs {cost} stars, {perLevel} more per level above 1 and {perHacked} more for every place hacked before. Possible from round {first}, at most one hack per turn, never on enemy cities and not while a foreign unit stands on the place. Hack tower ({tcost} stars, one per city, at most {tmax}, at least {spacing} tiles apart, built on a free tile in own territory): takes over one visible hostile vehicle or flyer within {reach} tiles (no ships, wonders, bosses, guided missiles, no unit standing in a city). NEXUS controls it at once and in its next turn ({rounds} turns); it may move and fight, but not capture, enter cities, embark, build or upgrade, and costs nobody upkeep. At the end of the NEXUS turn it returns to its owner, exhausted, with its remaining HP; with a {keep} % chance it stays with NEXUS for good instead (permanently taken over, a normal NEXUS unit with upkeep and city slot), with a {off} % chance it shuts down (destroyed, wreck, no stars for anyone). If the tower is destroyed, it returns at once. The tower recharges {cd} rounds from the takeover. City hack: NEXUS can also hack an explored enemy city without capturing it (at least one data centre, {ccost} stars, one every {ccd} rounds, need not be visible): for {crounds} rounds it sees every unit within the city radius plus {cr} tiles, also under the clouds, the tiles are revealed and the city panel shows the owner's treasury, the city income and its units. The owner is told and sees the hack marker on the city.

lore.title: {name}: Story

text.korvat: People's League of Korvat, humans. Leader: Grand Marshal Ilja Brodnik. Mass armies, red banners, choir song. Born from a hundred farming cooperatives of the steppe. In the League every ploughman is also a soldier. Brodnik, once a tractor driver, leads with iron paternalism. Furrows become front lines.
text.zyrr: Zyrr Swarm, alien race. Swarm Mother Xyl'Tharra. Once the Zyrr Swarm was only a scouting force, a vanguard searching for new worlds. But over the desert their mothership crashed, badly damaged. Instead of retreating, the Zyrr did the unthinkable: they began to change the world. Led by Swarm Mother Xyl'Tharra, an emergency landing site became a new home, the second world of the Zyrr Swarm.
text.vesper: Cult of the Final Hour, fanatics. Prophet Malachar. Robes, bone masks, bells, flames. At dusty pilgrimage sites the desperate gathered, the exiled, the sick, the guilty and the lost, waiting for the end of the world, for the Final Hour in which everything old passes away. From these gatherings rose Malachar, the prophet. He proclaimed: the end is no catastrophe, it is salvation. The cult needs no cities, no industry and no laws, only fire, faith and the certainty that the Final Hour will come. What it finds, it plunders; whoever listens joins the horde.
text.dravon: Protectorate of Dravon, humans. Commander Sarek Voss. Drill, camouflage green, balaclavas, barracks state. Mercenary companies guarded the ore mines of the desert, for anyone who paid. When the Standstill came, nobody paid anymore. The mercenaries kept the mines. Camps became barracks, barracks became a state. Nobody has ever seen Voss without his balaclava. In Dravon every recruit becomes a veteran, or is forgotten.
text.nexus: AI Collective NEXUS, machines. Primary Instance KERN-0. Robots, data centres, research, cyan light. Once NEXUS was only the logistics program of a mighty great power, built to coordinate supply chains, production and research. But when the humans left, it did not shut down. NEXUS simply kept calculating, optimising, learning and expanding. The former program became the AI Collective NEXUS. Led by KERN-0 it now coordinates research, production and expansion, efficient, logical, tireless. For NEXUS there are no coincidences, no dogmas and no nations, only data, resources and the most efficient solution for a stable future.
text.alvenia: Holy Alvenia, humans. High Priestess Liora Valen. An order of clerics, the sun halo, Light Wardens, Judgement. In the green hill valleys an order sings beneath the sun halo. Valen was a field doctor. She has seen what front lines do and believes in the redemption of the fallen. Whoever plunders, burns or converts will meet her Judgement. The Order is the counterweight to the cult.
text.velkar: Technocracy of Velkar, humans. Director Aurel Kesh. Production, labs, pioneers, cold. In the icy north the empire's old polar laboratory survived the Standstill. Kesh proclaimed the technocracy: the formula decides, not the people. Velkar's pioneers build fortresses where others freeze. Their dream: endless energy. Whoever ends scarcity, the world will follow.
text.meridon: Trade League of Meridon, humans. Admiral Coralie Nerezza. Harbours, gold, fog, spies, shadow fleet. Rich harbour cities buy each other's debts until a league is born, before the Great Standstill the leading nation in culture, economy, stock exchanges and finance. Its speculation helped to trigger the collapse. After the New Order and the shooting down of the spaceship the elite fled to the sea and bought whole fleets. Nerezza bought her first cruiser with smuggled gold and has not lost a bet since. Her spies know everything before it happens. The League works in secret; its old counting houses once gave rise to the Verdan empire. Meridon does not want to conquer the world, but to buy it.

lore.prologueText: Once the empire of Verdan ruled the whole continent with machines. Then the Great Standstill: overnight all the lights went out. Rusting wrecks recall the war that followed. For two generations, borders drawn in chalk on old maps held. Until the sky burned: the Zyrr mothership crashes into the desert, the bell tolls by itself, and the front begins to move again.

goal.text: Points mode: after {rounds} rounds the highest score wins (medal at the top). Points come from explored tiles ({tile}), territory tiles ({territory}), city levels ({level}), doctrines ({tech} per tier) and more. Conquest: the last side holding cities wins. turn.text: All factions take turns one after another; a round ends when everyone has moved. At the start of your turn stars come in: {city} per city level, {hq} extra for the headquarters, plus bonuses from buildings, rewards and embassies. Stars are the only currency for units, buildings, production sites, doctrines and upgrades. You start with {start} stars.

Infantry, MG, snipers and pioneers (Light Wardens and railgun marksmen too) defend ×{outpost} on an own outpost. With the matching doctrine, forests, mountains and (for ships) coasts defend ×{terrain}. Troops and tanks in forests or cities also defend ×{ranged} against ranged attacks from two or more tiles. Fliers get no cover. The tile panel shows the cover.

cities.title: Cities & production
cities.text: Move a unit onto a settlement or enemy city; at the start of your next turn you can capture it. Buildings on resources in the city area add population, a full population raises the city level: more income, more units and a reward. With every level the city territory grows by up to {grow} free tiles in the next ring, nearest first, up to at most {max} x {max} tiles; foreign territory stays foreign. Transmitter towers (in the campaign; in free games bases stand there) are neutral places: they train troops and bring {towerInc} stars per round, but do not grow. Every city has {slots} slots for upgrades. Every upgrade also raises the unit limit by {cap}. Buy level: for {buy} × (level + 1) stars a city rises one level at once (level 1 → 2: {ex2}, 2 → 3: {ex3}, 3 → 4: {ex4}), with the usual reward; once per city and round, not for transmitter towers, supply lines or the cult. Units come from production sites in the city territory (see below). Doctrines unlock buildings and upgrades, bring advantages and get dearer with every city: tier 1 costs {t1} stars with one city, {t1c3} with three cities, tier 3 costs {t3c3} with three cities. The tile panel shows locked buildings with “Requires: …”.

factions.text: Can be switched off in the setup. It needs the faction's own victory doctrine (tier 3), drawn with a dashed rim in the doctrine tree. The victory tracker in the menu shows the progress of all known factions.

ships.text: Every city with water in its territory or right next to the city tile buys ships under “Troops”; they launch empty on a free water tile at the city (shallow first, ocean only with diving). The landing boat costs {boat} stars and needs no base: a land unit moves onto it from an adjacent tile, boards and is ferried across. An empty ship has hull HP ({hull} for the boat) and cannot go ashore; the empty boat does not attack. Warships cost their upgrade price and need {base} or {dock} in the city. The cult and NEXUS need {tech} for boats; the Zyrr wade and have no ships. As before: at an own {base} a land unit becomes a landing boat for free, ships upgrade in own territory, and whoever moves ashore becomes the carried unit again.

Instead of a blow he can blow himself up next to a ground target: {blastArmour} damage to armour, {blastOther} to other ground units, without a roll or return fire; he is dead afterwards (counts for martyrdom). academy.liftDesc: The academy lifts off and floats after {academyLift} round; then it moves {academyMove} tiles per turn. No production until landing. While floating, only flyers, flak and tanks can attack it.
academy.moveDesc: Tap a target on the map: up to {n} tiles, over water and mountains too.
academy.moveHint: Tap a highlighted tile to move the academy there.
academy.landDesc: Terraforms for {academyTerraform} round and lands at the start of the next turn; until then it keeps floating (same attack rules) and does not move. {into} The tile and free surroundings become academy territory. It trains again in the landing turn.
academy.shieldDesc: {academyShieldHp} HP. Absorbs attacks on the academy and on units on its tile first, on the ground and in the air, even without a garrison. Recharges {academyShieldRegen} HP per turn; once destroyed, it can be rebuilt after {academyShieldRebuild} rounds.
academy.attackDesc: No return fire: the academy only fires its neutron beam in its own turn. On the ground without shield and hull it is captured like any city.
academy.postDesc: Captured place: one tile, gives stars and vision, trains nothing. Territory and growth pass to the academy.
academy.toastPost: {city} is now a research post: +{pop} population for the academy
academy.slotsUsed: All {max} trainings of this round used or no free tile at the academy.
academy.razeDesc: Neutral place will be levelled: {city} vanishes, its territory becomes academy territory. No capture, no reward. Then like terraform and land: {academyTerraform} round, landing next turn.
academy.razeConfirm: Neutral place will be levelled: {city} vanishes for good instead of being captured as a research post. Terraform anyway?
academy.cancelDesc: The academy keeps floating; this turn's tiles are used up.
academy.landTargetsHint: Highlighted tiles: landing possible (tap a target to move there).
academy.toastAbort: {city}: landing cancelled, the tile is no longer free
academy.terraformNext: Lands at the start of the next turn, production from the turn after.
academy.terraformFlat: The tile is already plain grassland.
academy.beamDesc: Fires at a visible hostile unit or hostile structure (gun, silo, hack tower) within {academyBeamRange} tiles: a full hit deals {academyBeamDamage} damage, weaker hits less, a miss nothing. Built in it fires every {academyBeamEvery} turns, with the beam amplifier every turn. No return fire, no cities. On the ground, floating and while terraforming, not in the lift-off round; independent of training.
academy.beamPick: Tap a target in range (marked red), tap it again to fire.
academy.beamNone: No visible hostile target within {academyBeamRange} tiles.
academy.strategies: Two ways: build a typical army, or expand the academy into a flying fortress (shield, defence missiles, armour, beam), hold out until then and attack with it.

shield.name: Shield boost
shield.desc: Per level +{academyModShieldHp} shield HP and +{academyModShieldRegen} recharge per turn (now {hp} HP, {regen} per turn); a standing shield grows at once. The base shield is built as before.

missiles.name: Defence missiles
missiles.desc: Level {n}: {n} interceptions between two own turns. Intercepted are attacks by flyers (drones and guided missiles too) and mech rockets on the academy and own units on or next to it (no damage, no return fire) and rocket silo strikes hitting it or an adjacent tile. Ground fire, round fire of guns and flak is not.

armour.name: Armour
armour.desc: Hull with {hp} HP ({academyModArmourHp} per level), recharges {academyModArmourRegen} HP per turn. What gets through the shield hits the hull; only without a hull does a hit in the air force the emergency landing, and on the ground the academy can only be captured without shield and hull.

beam.name: Beam amplifier
beam.desc: The neutron beam fires every turn instead of every {academyBeamEvery} turns. Damage ({academyBeamDamage}) and range ({academyBeamRange} tiles) stay.

beam.name: Beam relay
beam.buildDesc: Teleporter on this post: once per round a unit can be beamed here from the academy. It is in transit for one round and arrives ready at the start of the next turn.
beam.actionDesc: The unit vanishes and appears at the start of the next turn at the relay in {city}, ready for action.
beam.toastReturn: {unit}: relay lost, back at the academy

place.desc: Take over this neutral place remotely, as if a unit had captured it. Costs {cost} stars and one hack charge. Every data centre in your territory gives one charge, which recharges {recharge} rounds after a hack.
place.noDc: Build a data centre first: every data centre gives one hack charge.
place.visibleOnly: Only places you have revealed can be hacked.
place.toastOwn: {city} hacked: it now belongs to the collective.

tower.name: Hack tower
tower.desc: Structure of {name}, not a unit: impassable, no return fire, never fires on its own. Takes over one visible hostile vehicle or flyer within {towerReach} tiles for {towerRounds} turns: it obeys at once and in the next turn, then returns to its owner, exhausted, with its remaining HP, unless it stays with NEXUS for good ({towerKeep} % chance, permanently taken over) or shuts down ({towerShutdown} % chance, destroyed as a wreck). It cannot capture, embark, build or upgrade and costs nobody upkeep. One unit per tower, the tower recharges {towerCooldown} rounds from the takeover. If the tower falls, the unit returns at once. If the territory is lost, the tower is razed.
tower.buildDesc: Build a hack tower here ({towerCost} stars): it takes over hostile vehicles and flyers within {towerReach} tiles for {towerRounds} turns. At most one per own city and {towerMax} in total, at least {towerSpacing} tiles apart.
tower.limit: Limit reached: one hack tower per city, at most {towerMax}.
tower.spacing: Too close to another own hack tower (at least {towerSpacing} tiles).
tower.title: Take over unit
tower.pick: Tap a highlighted hostile vehicle or flyer within {reach} tiles.
tower.none: No hostile vehicle or flyer within {reach} tiles.
tower.confirm: Tap again or press Take over.
tower.lost: Hack tower razed: the territory was lost.

hijack.desc: Controlled by {name} until the end of its turn in round {round}. It may move and fight, but not capture, embark, build or upgrade, and costs nobody upkeep. Afterwards it returns with its remaining HP.
hijack.toastVictim: {name} hacked your {unit}! It returns after {n} of their turns.
hijack.backTower: Hack tower destroyed: {unit} is back under your command.
hijack.lostUnit: {unit} broke down: its owner is gone.
hijack.kept: {unit} of {name} permanently taken over: it now belongs to the collective.
hijack.shutdown: {unit} of {name} shut down after the takeover.
hijack.shutdownVictim: Your {unit} shut down after the hack and is destroyed.
hijack.chance: At the end: {keep} % chance it stays with {name} for good, {off} % chance it shuts down (wreck).

city.desc: Hack this enemy city, do not capture it: for {cityRounds} rounds you see every unit within {r} tiles, even under the clouds, the tiles are revealed and the city panel shows its data. Costs {cityCost} stars, one city hack every {cityCooldown} rounds.
city.toastOwn: {city} of {name} hacked: you see the city for {n} rounds.
city.toastVictim: {name} hacked your city {city}! They see it for {n} rounds.

spark.name: Divine Spark
spark.title: Divine Spark: pick a target
spark.pick: Tap a tile {min} to {range} tiles away: the {w}×{h} area forms around it. A spotter must stand at most {spot} tiles from it.
spark.confirm: Tap again or press Fire! Esc cancels.
spark.noHits: No visible targets in the area
spark.own: Warning: {n} own units in the target
spark.own1: Warning: 1 own unit in the target
spark.blocked: Blocked: the area holds units of a faction you are not at war with.
spark.outOfRange: Too far: the whole area must lie at most {range} tiles from the gun.
spark.statDesc: Area shot: {dmg} damage per target on a full hit (hit luck as with every shot), on {w}×{h} tiles, own units included.
spark.rangeDesc: The whole area lies {min} to {range} tiles from the gun: it never hits itself or its adjacent tiles.
spark.cooldownDesc: {cd} rounds of reloading after every shot.
spark.defencelessDesc: Does not strike back and has hardly any defence: keep it behind your own line.
spark.rule: Divine Spark (Alvenia): giant gun from the foundry, at most {sparkMax} at a time, {sparkCost} stars, upkeep {sparkUpkeep} per round. It does not attack like other units but hurls a spark onto an area of {sparkW}×{sparkH} tiles via the action "Hurl spark". The whole area must lie {sparkMin} to {sparkRange} tiles from the gun (it never hits itself or its adjacent tiles), and another own unit or an own city must stand at most {sparkSpot} tiles from the area (or a radar sweep or sighting reveals it). Every target in the area rolls its own hit luck on {sparkDmg} damage, own units included; cover and defence do not count. Units of a faction you are not at war with block the shot. The spark fires only from a standstill: not in a turn in which it has moved, and it does not move afterwards. Then it recharges for {sparkCd} rounds. In close combat it is defenceless (defence {sparkDef}, no return fire).
